summary: The core area is the FastAPI foundation every route rides on: pydantic-settings config (~200 env-backed fields, many of them only defaults for Mongo-backed runtime_config overrides), app assembly and a lifespan that opens Mongo/Redis/Postgres, runs one-time index migrations and backfills, and starts about 20 background loops. It also covers a 9-layer middleware stack (gzip, two CORS layers, request id, api-host 301, security headers, CSP and body caps, idempotency, usage, HEAD), one JSON error envelope, Redis sliding-window rate limiting with a Mongo fallback, and two separate account systems: dev-portal email/password/GitHub with JWT, refresh sessions and API tokens, and site Discord-only accounts with HttpOnly cookies. The rest is the email outbox, usage metrics, GitHub secret-scanning auto-revoke, and the Docker/compose wiring for the api/web/bot/builder containers that share one image. It is about 10k lines of Python and nothing here calls kiwi_native yet. Most of it ports directly to axum + mongodb + redis + tokio-postgres. The real cost is wire-compatibility: pydantic vs jsonable_encoder datetime formats, Python float repr, the Starlette CORS and middleware header semantics, the FastAPI-generated /openapi.json with its markers, and auth artifacts (argon2 PHC, PyJWT, the custom-alphabet API token checksum) that must keep validating across a mixed Python/Rust cutover.

components.name: App assembly, lifespan and OpenAPI (app/main.py)

Redis: PING at startup
Postgres: pool + pg_schema.init for leaderboards, market, codexes
Disk: {site_root}/static existence check (site/ bind mount, /app/site ro) decides whether site_router is mounted
runtime_config feature_* flags (read at /openapi.json request time to prune ops)
python_deps: uvicorn[standard] (--proxy-headers, --forwarded-allow-ips, --workers N, --timeout-graceful-shutdown 3) -> hyper/tokio + a custom X-Forwarded-For layer + graceful shutdown with a 3s cutoff
fastapi.openapi.utils.get_openapi -> utoipa (per-route annotations) or a frozen exported spec JSON
background: Startup, in order: configure_logging; warn if SECRET_KEY is the default or CAPTCHA_SECRET is unset; init_db; init_redis; init_postgres; bootstrap_admin; seed_interest_items_if_empty (market); seed_supporters_if_empty; backfill_owner_handles + backfill_takedown_artifacts (mods hub, the latter try/except); backfill_modpack_handles

Spawned per uvicorn worker: usage_recorder, email worker (10s poll), news (1800s), feeds (300s), events (900s), mod_stats, steam_workshop (21600s), chaos (1800s), status prober (60s), delve, btt_releases (1800s), update archiver (1200s probe, off unless TROVE_UPDATE_ENABLED), cheaters warmer, giveaway worker (60s), SSE event bus (Redis pub/sub + 30s watcher), event scheduler, webhook BRPOP consumer, DM BRPOP consumer, maintenance_loop (86400s)
Shutdown stops them in reverse, then closes Redis, Postgres and Mongo
components.port_notes: Single axum Router that merges every feature router with its prefix. Router-level feature gates (Depends(require_X_enabled)) run BEFORE endpoint auth dependencies, so a disabled feature returns 404 before any 401/403; keep that order. site_router is only included when {site_root}/static exists. Python runs N uvicorn workers: the prod overlay sets --workers ${API_WORKERS:-8} and the local .env has API_WORKERS=12. deploy.sh runs plain `docker compose up`, so the overlay only applies if COMPOSE_FILE is set on the server. Every lifespan loop therefore runs N times today. A single multi-threaded tokio process turns them into singletons: fine for the claim-based ones (email outbox, BRPOP), better for the duplicated ones (maintenance), and it changes per-process caches (runtime_config 5s, GitHub keys) into global ones. /openapi.json starts from FastAPI's generated spec (openapi 3.1.x, info.title=settings.app_name 'Kiwi API', version '1.0.0', description=API_DESCRIPTION markdown, tags in API_TAGS order with a long description only on 'creators', servers=[{url: api_url, description: 'Production'}], components.securitySchemes SessionJWT/APIToken/SiteSessionJWT as HTTP bearer). It is then post-processed: (a) ops whose dependency tree contains a public_scope checker, or with x-tokenless: true, get the summary prefixed '🔓 ' (once), description += _TOKENLESS_NOTE, and security = [{}, ...existing]; (b) else ops containing require_master_ingest get '⭐ ' plus _MASTER_NOTE; (c) the APIToken scheme description gets the 🔓/⭐ sentence appended. At request time, ops whose route carries a feature-gate dependency are removed when that flag is OFF, and a path whose last op is removed is dropped. Only include_in_schema routes appear (auth/tokens/site-auth/admin are hidden). Byte-parity needs utoipa schemas that mirror every pydantic model, or a build-time export of the Python spec plus a (path, method) -> flag table for pruning. The Redoc docs site depends on this. FastAPI's default /docs and /redoc routes still exist but are dead under the API CSP (their CDN scripts are blocked); they can be dropped. /config returns PublicConfig in field order app_name, api_url, captcha_provider, captcha_sitekey (null), require_verified_for_tokens, scopes[{key,bit,resource,description}], token_creation_daily_limit, revoke_reasons [4 fixed strings], github_oauth_enabled, discord_oauth_enabled. /health returns {"status":"ok"}. /api-info is an inline f-string HTML card. All JSON is Starlette JSONResponse: json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False, separators=(',',':')).

components.name: Settings / env config
data: .env in CWD (utf-8, extra keys ignored)
python_deps: pydantic-settings -> serde + figment (Env + dotenvy) or envy
components.port_notes: One flat Settings struct with the same field names. Env lookup is case-insensitive (SECRET_KEY -> secret_key). List fields (cors_origins) are parsed from env as JSON. Bools accept true/false/1/0/yes/no/on/off. captcha_provider is Literal['hcaptcha','turnstile']. Derived properties to reproduce: github_oauth_enabled (id AND secret), discord_oauth_enabled, discord_install_link (install_url, else https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=..), postgres_enabled, email_enabled (smtp_host set), asset_url ((asset_base_url or app_url).rstrip('/')). Key defaults: secret_key 'CHANGE_ME_insecure_dev_secret_do_not_use_in_production', jwt HS256, access 15 min, refresh 30 days, api_token_prefix 'kiwi', mongo_uri mongodb://localhost:27016, mongo_db kiwi, redis_url None, postgres pool 2..10, the body caps, api_url/dev_url/docs_url/app_url (api./dev./docs./trove.aallyn.net), internal_api_url http://api:8000, internal_key '', backlog_dir /data/backlog (absolute on purpose), site_root 'site'. Many fields (rate limits, cheater/rename/duplicate tunables, class-activity thresholds, status prober hosts) are only the DEFAULTS of app/admin/runtime_config REGISTRY entries. Live values come from the Mongo runtime_config collection (value stored as a JSON string, 5s per-process cache), so the Rust foundation must ship runtime_config.get_setting/get_rate_limit alongside Settings. Some settings are stale or doc-only (e.g. the docstring says Discord scope 'identify email guilds' but the code requests 'identify guilds').

components.name: Middleware stack (gzip, CORS x2, request-id, api-host 301, security/CSP/body caps, HEAD)
data: Disk: site/static (sha256 of files for ?v= hashing; api container /app/site:ro)
runtime_config 'embed.allowed_origins' via app.embed.service.allowed_origins() (memoised ~30s, fails closed) for the /embed/viewer CSP
python_deps: Starlette BaseHTTPMiddleware/ASGI middleware -> tower Layers / axum middleware::from_fn
starlette CORSMiddleware -> custom tower layer (tower-http CorsLayer differs)
contextvars request id -> tokio::task_local! + tracing span
components.port_notes: Execution order, outer to inner: ResponseCompression -> PublicAssetCors -> Starlette CORS -> request_context -> api_host_redirect -> security -> idempotency -> usage -> HEAD->GET -> exception handlers -> router. request_context: rid = the incoming X-Request-ID verbatim (not validated) or 'req_'+16 hex chars; it is bound for log lines and error bodies, the response X-Request-ID is always overwritten, and any unhandled error becomes the 500 envelope inside CORS. api_host_redirect: hosts = api_url host plus apex and www.apex when it has 3 or more labels, minus the app_url host (prod: api.aallyn.net, aallyn.net, www.aallyn.net), matched against the lowercased Host. GET/HEAD to a site page (exact page-path set or prefix /mods/ /modpacks/ /player/ /drop/ /swf-docs/) gets a 301 to app_url+path+?query. That 301 carries no security headers. security: the body cap is checked from Content-Length ONLY (a chunked body bypasses it; a non-integer value is ignored). Caps: /git/* 100MiB, /v1/mods/* 20MiB, =/v1/leaderboards/insert 20MiB, =/v1/market/insert 20MiB, =/v1/ocr/character 12MiB, =/site/sound-studio/build 32MiB, /site/blueprint-editor/* 64MiB, =/site/unlock-debug 160MiB, /site/mod-workshop/* 32MiB, /site/drops/* 512MiB, =/v1/misc/feedback 24MiB, default 8MiB. Over the cap: 413 envelope with code 'bad_request' and message 'Request body exceeds the {N}-byte limit', returned before any security header is added. Then setdefault (a route-set value wins): X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Strict-Transport-Security 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains', Permissions-Policy 'geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()'. Path exactly /embed/viewer: delete X-Frame-Options, setdefault CSP = SITE_CSP minus frame-ancestors + '; frame-ancestors <origins space-joined | 'none'>', setdefault Cache-Control no-cache, and return early (no credential rule). Otherwise X-Frame-Options DENY, and CSP = SITE_CSP for site paths (exact page set, /static/, /site/, page prefixes) else API_CSP; copy both strings byte-exact from csp.py. /static/*: Cache-Control is OVERWRITTEN with 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable' when ?v equals sha256(file)[:10], 'public, max-age=604800' for .woff2, else 'no-cache'. Page paths: setdefault no-cache. Finally, if the REQUEST has any Authorization header (any scheme) or a kiwi_site_access cookie, and the path is not a public asset (/site/rigs/*, /site/dressing/*, =/site/render/brdf-map.png, =/site/codexes/render): OVERWRITE Cache-Control 'private, no-store' and merge Vary 'Cookie, Authorization' (case-insensitive de-dupe, joined with ', '). Exact page-path set: / /app /browse /documentation /commands /leaderboards /updates /support /login /dashboard /market /store /codexes /codexes/crafting /status /giveaways /activity /class-activity /clubs /terms /privacy /accessibility /changelog /mods /modpacks /server-time /swf-docs /calendar /streams /releases /classes /star-chart /gem-simulator /gem-evaluator /gem-builds /calculators /gems-guide /abilities /gem-abilities /guides /gem-tools /allies /fishing-guide /gear-guide /loot-collector-guide /dressing-room /sound-studio /mod-workshop /tomes /blueprint-editor /unlock-debug /unlock_debug /search /zakros-ui-requests /zakros-ui-stats /community-sites. New pages must be added here; share one Rust module with the web binary. CORS (Starlette): an origin is allowed if it is in cors_origins (https://docs.aallyn.net, https://dev.aallyn.net, http://localhost|127.0.0.1 on :25468 and :15546) or fullmatches `https://([a-z0-9-]+\.)?aallyn\.net|http://(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)(:\d+)?`. Credentials true. A preflight (OPTIONS + Origin + Access-Control-Request-Method) is answered by the middleware: 200 text/plain 'OK' with ACAO=<origin>, Allow-Methods 'DELETE, GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PATCH, POST, PUT', Allow-Headers = the echoed request headers, Max-Age 600, Allow-Credentials true, Vary Origin; a bad origin or method gets 400 'Disallowed CORS origin' (etc.). Simple requests from allowed origins get ACAO echo + ACAC true + Access-Control-Expose-Headers 'X-Request-ID, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, Retry-After, X-Dressing-Dropped, Content-Disposition' + Vary Origin; disallowed origins get nothing. PublicAssetCors applies to public-asset paths only when the Origin is NOT one of ours: OPTIONS -> 204 with ACAO *, Allow-Methods 'GET, HEAD, OPTIONS', Allow-Headers *, Max-Age 86400; otherwise strip ACAO/ACAC/ACEH, collapse every Vary into one header that includes Origin, add ACAO * and ACEH X-Dressing-Dropped. Compression (outermost): only when the request's accept-encoding contains 'gzip'; status 2xx/3xx except 204/206/304; no Content-Encoding or Content-Range; media type in {application/javascript, application/json, application/manifest+json, application/x-ndjson, application/xml, image/svg+xml, text/css, text/csv, text/html, text/javascript, text/markdown, text/plain, text/xml} (never text/event-stream); declared Content-Length >= 1024. A single-chunk body < 1024 bytes, or one that doesn't shrink, is sent raw. Otherwise gzip level 5 with the exact Content-Length and Vary += Accept-Encoding. A multi-chunk body is stream-gzipped with Content-Length removed. Uncompressed responses get NO Vary: Accept-Encoding (the edge cache keys on URL only); decide consciously whether to keep that. HEAD: rewritten to GET for routing except /v1/events* (would open an endless SSE). axum's get() already answers HEAD, so just make HEAD on the SSE route 405 and keep usage accounting GET-only. Logging format: '%(asctime)s %(levelname)-7s %(name)s [rid=..] msg', datefmt %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z. The web container reuses add_head_method/add_security/add_request_context plus a StaticCompressionMiddleware (Starlette GZip, min 1024, paths ending .css .js .json .svg .txt .map .md) and the geo maintenance gate (app/geo_maintenance/gate.py: 503 HTML + Retry-After 120 for listed countries, list fetched from the api /internal/geo-maintenance with X-Internal-Key).

components.name: Error envelope and codes
python_deps: fastapi exception handlers -> axum IntoResponse for an ApiError type + a rejection mapper for extractors
components.port_notes: Every error body is {"error":{"code":..,"message":..,"details":<any|null>,"request_id":"req_.."|"-"}} in that key order, compact JSON, ensure_ascii=False. Codes: bad_request, validation_error, not_authenticated, invalid_credentials, captcha_failed, forbidden, not_found, not_public, conflict, email_taken, email_unverified, disposable_email, password_breached, account_locked, insufficient_scope, ip_not_allowed, rate_limited, method_not_allowed, service_unavailable, internal_error (other areas also pass ad-hoc string codes). APIError renders with its own headers (WWW-Authenticate: Bearer on auth 401s; Retry-After + X-RateLimit-* on 429; Retry-After on account_locked). Framework HTTPException maps status to code {400 bad_request, 401 not_authenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not_found, 405 method_not_allowed, 409 conflict, 422 validation_error, 429 rate_limited, 503 service_unavailable, otherwise internal_error}. The message is Starlette's phrase: an unknown route gives 'Not Found'; a wrong method gives 'Method Not Allowed' plus an Allow header. Framework 404s on GET/HEAD whose path does NOT start with /v1/, /v1, /admin, /site/, /git/, /secret-scanning, /openapi, /.well-known, /health, /config or /metrics, and whose Accept contains 'text/html', return the themed HTML _NOT_FOUND_HTML (copy byte-exact, including the inline data: favicon). APIError 404s (feature gates, lookups) are ALWAYS JSON. A 422 from request validation has message 'Request validation failed' and details = the pydantic v2 errors list [{type, loc, msg, input, ctx?}] (url excluded). FastAPI also returns 422 (type json_invalid), not 400, for malformed JSON bodies, and for bad path params such as an invalid ObjectId. Reproducing details byte-for-byte from serde rejections is impractical; keep code/status/message identical and emulate the loc/type shape. Unhandled errors give 500 internal_error 'Internal server error' and are logged. raise_from_value_error: a message containing 'already exists' gives 409 conflict, else 400 bad_request. COMMON_ERROR_RESPONSES/error_responses() only document 400/401/403/404/422/429 in OpenAPI.

components.name: Rate limiting + login lockout
data: Redis: rl:{key} ZSET (sliding window); keys used: token:{token_id}, token:{bucket}:{token_id}, public:{ip}, public:{bucket}:{ip}, ingest:{route_template}:{token_id}, signup:{ip}, login:{ip}, resend:{ip}, forgot:{ip}, tokencreate:{user_id} (+ other areas' keys)
Redis: loginfail:{email_lower} (INCR, EXPIRE window), loginlock:{email_lower} ('1' EX lockout)
Mongo: rate_limit_buckets (raw, not Beanie) {_id:'{key}:{window_start}', count, expires_at}; TTL index on expires_at expireAfterSeconds=0 (Redis-unset fallback)
python_deps: redis-py eval -> redis crate Script (EVALSHA with EVAL fallback)
components.port_notes: Copy the sliding-window Lua script exactly: ZREMRANGEBYSCORE key 0 now-window; ZADD now member; count = ZCARD; PEXPIRE ceil(window*1000); if count > limit then ZREM member; return count. now is a float of epoch seconds sent as str(time.time()). member = f'{now:.6f}:{seq}' with a process-local seq mod 1e6 (needs a uniqueness source per process). 429 when count > max. Headers: X-RateLimit-Limit = max; X-RateLimit-Remaining = max(0, max-count); X-RateLimit-Reset = int(now + window), which in Redis mode is NOT a real window end. Retry-After = max(1, int(reset-now)), effectively ~window. 429 body details {limit, window_seconds}, message 'Rate limit exceeded. Slow down and try again later.'. Mongo fallback: fixed window, window_start = floor(now/window)*window, find_one_and_update {$inc count, $setOnInsert expires_at=window end} upsert, reset = window end. Limits come from runtime_config.get_rate_limit(prefix) as (prefix_max, prefix_window_seconds) for api_rate_limit, public_anon_rate_limit, signup_rate_limit, login_rate_limit, forgot_password_rate_limit and ingest_cooldown. resend (5/3600) and tokencreate (token_creation_daily_limit/86400) are hard-coded or settings. Keep the key strings identical so Python and Rust share budgets during a mixed cutover. Client IP = uvicorn's proxy-header result (rightmost untrusted X-Forwarded-For entry when the peer is in FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS), and 'unknown' when absent. Success headers are set on FastAPI's injected Response, so they appear ONLY on endpoints that return a model/dict, not on ones that return a Response object (downloads, PNGs, HTML). Lockout uses settings directly (login_max_attempts 5, window 900, lockout 900): INCR loginfail, EXPIRE on the first failure; at >= max SET loginlock EX; a lock returns 429 account_locked with Retry-After = TTL; success DELs both keys. Without Redis, lockout is a silent no-op.

components.name: Idempotency-Key middleware
data: Redis: idem:{sha256hex(sha256(Authorization)[:16]:METHOD:path:key)} = '{"s":"lock"}' EX 60 or {"s":"done","c":status,"ct":content-type,"b":base64 body} EX 86400
python_deps: redis SET NX EX / GET / DEL -> redis crate
components.port_notes: Active only when an Idempotency-Key header is present (len <= 200), the method is POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, and Redis is configured. It fails open on any Redis error. Claim with SET NX EX idempotency_lock_seconds. If the key exists and the record is 'done', replay: body = b64 body, status c, media type ct, and ONLY the header Idempotent-Replay: true. The original headers (rate-limit, Set-Cookie, Content-Disposition) are NOT replayed. If the record is still 'lock': 409 conflict 'A request with this Idempotency-Key is already in progress.'. On the first run the whole body is buffered. A 2xx stores the record for idempotency_result_seconds; anything else DELs the key. The response is rebuilt with headers=dict(response.headers), which collapses duplicate headers (multiple Set-Cookie become the first one) and is a latent bug to fix rather than copy. The namespace hashes only the Authorization header, so all cookie-authenticated callers share the empty-credential namespace. It sits inside security (replays get security headers) and outside usage (replays aren't double-counted). JSON is the Python json.dumps default ({"s": "done", "c": ...} with spaces) when written by Python. Rust must read both spacings and should write compatible JSON.

components.name: Auth primitives + request dependencies (JWT, API tokens, scopes, IP hash, passwords, captcha, HIBP)
data: Mongo users (lookup by _id), api_tokens (lookup by hashed_token)
Redis via ratelimit + tokens/usage
Outbound: api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/{5 hex} (Add-Padding: true, 5s, fail-open), Turnstile/hCaptcha siteverify (form secret/response/remoteip, 10s)
python_deps: argon2-cffi PasswordHasher() -> argon2 crate with explicit Params(m=65536,t=3,p=4,len 32) Argon2id v19
hashlib sha256/sha1, hmac, zlib.crc32 -> sha2, sha1, hmac, crc32fast
components.port_notes: Passwords: argon2-cffi defaults give $argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$<salt16>$<hash32> PHC strings. The Rust argon2 crate's defaults differ (m=19456,t=2,p=1), so set the params explicitly; verify reads params from the PHC string; any error means false. Session JWT (dev portal): HS256 over settings.secret_key, claims {sub:user_id, ver:token_version, iat, exp(+15m), type:'access', sid:session_id}. iat/exp are int seconds; the header is {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}. Decoding verifies exp with 0 leeway and rejects a non-int or future iat. jsonwebtoken defaults to a 60s leeway, so set leeway=0, and check iat manually. type is NOT checked on decode, so purpose tokens (email_verify/password_reset/email_change, same key) are only rejected because their ver is missing; checking type=='access' in Rust is safe. Dev-portal auth rejects kind=='site' tokens, requires User.is_active and ver == token_version, and gives 401 'Invalid or expired session token' / 'Wrong-audience token' / 'Account is inactive or no longer exists' / 'Session has been ended; please log in again'. get_current_superuser returns 403 forbidden 'Administrator privileges required'. API token format: '{prefix}_{43-char body}_{checksum}', prefix 'kiwi'. The base62 ALPHABET is string.ascii_letters+digits = 'a-zA-Z0-9' (NOT 0-9A-Za-z). The checksum is base62 big-endian of zlib.crc32(body), unpadded, 1-6 chars. The display prefix is 'kiwi_'+body[:8]. Stored hashed_token = sha256_hex(full token). Validation: if the strict regex matches and the checksum fails, return 401 with no DB hit; if the shape doesn't match, fall back to the DB lookup (legacy tokens). Revoked returns 401 'Invalid or revoked API token'; expired (expires_at < now) returns 401 'API token has expired'. Bearer parsing follows FastAPI HTTPBearer(auto_error=False): a non-'bearer' scheme or empty credentials count as NO credential (so anonymous on public scopes), while the security middleware still treats any Authorization header as a credential for Cache-Control. Per-request token enforcement, in order: set request.state.usage_user_id/token_id (so 403/429 are still usage-recorded); IP allowlist (HMAC-SHA256(key=ip_salt ascii, msg=normalized ip) hex, compare_digest against allowed_ip_hashes, salt = token_urlsafe(16), CIDR rejected) giving 403 ip_not_allowed 'Requests from this IP are not allowed for this token'; rate limit; then record_token_use. require_scope(scope) gives 403 insufficient_scope 'This token is missing the required scope: {scope}'. public_scope(scope, rate_multiplier, bucket): no token means anon per-IP limit; a valid token WITH the scope gets the per-token limit with bucket = bucket or (scope if multiplier != 1); a valid token WITHOUT the scope is downgraded to anonymous; a bad token is a 401. require_master_ingest: a credential with exactly two '.' is treated as a session JWT, otherwise an API token with full limits; a non-superuser gets 403 'Master account required for ingest endpoints.'; the token path adds the cooldown key ingest:{route.path template}:{token_id}. Scope bitmask: permanent bits 0..16 (rotations:read 1, feeds:read 2, stats:read 4, gems:read 8, misc:read 16, mods:read 32, updates:read 64, codexes:read 128, btt:read 256, leaderboards:read 512, market:read 1024, activity:read 2048, giveaways:read 4096, events:read 8192, ocr:read 16384, store:read 32768, mods:write 65536). Mask 0 = all scopes, present and future. A valid mask uses only known bits. decode(0)=[]. Captcha is skipped (returns true) unless BOTH secret and sitekey are set; a missing token is false. HIBP: SHA-1 uppercase, 5-char prefix, suffix match, count; fail-open gives 0; a hit is 400 password_breached with details {breach_count}. client_ip = request.client.host after proxy-header rewrite. device_label UA heuristic (Edge > Opera > Firefox > Chrome > Safari; Windows > Android > iOS > macOS > Linux) gives 'Browser on OS'. utils.iso() emits Python isoformat ('+00:00', microseconds only if nonzero), unlike pydantic's 'Z'.

components.name: DB init: Mongo/Beanie bootstrap, Redis, Postgres pool, pagination
data: Mongo db 'kiwi': init_beanie over ~70 Documents (collections in this area: users, sessions, site_users, site_sessions, username_change_requests, api_tokens, usage_events, email_outbox, runtime_config; plus every feature's collections, e.g. page_views, mod_projects, mod_releases, mod_download_events, giveaways, prize_codes)
Mongo raw: rate_limit_buckets (TTL expires_at), system_state

TTL indexes named '{field}_ttl': usage_events.created_at (usage_retention_days*86400), page_views.created_at (pageview_retention_days*86400), email_outbox.created_at (30d), mod_download_events.created_at (8d), sessions.expires_at (0), site_sessions.expires_at (0)
Index drops: mod_projects.source_1_source_id_1 (before Beanie; re-created as partial), mod_releases.project_id_1_tag_1, mod_projects.slug_1, site_users.email_1

One-off data fixes: $unset ip/user_agent on sessions+site_sessions; $unset discord_guilds/_synced_at and email on site_users; $unset winner_email on giveaways, awarded_to_email on prize_codes; backfills mod_projects.last_release_at, mod_projects.issues_enabled (true only for owner_handle 'aallyn'), mod_releases.announced_at (pipeline $ifNull published_at/created_at)
Redis: from_url(REDIS_URL, decode_responses=True), PING at startup
Postgres (asyncpg pool min 2 / max 10 per worker, command_timeout 120, jsonb codec json.dumps/json.loads), schema init: app/trove/leaderboards/pg_schema, market/pg_schema, codexes/pg_schema
python_deps: beanie 2.1 + pymongo AsyncMongoClient(tz_aware=True) -> mongodb crate + bson (chrono) with typed structs
asyncpg -> tokio-postgres + deadpool-postgres (COPY binary) or sqlx
components.port_notes: Beanie creates every model's Settings.indexes at boot (unique, compound, partialFilterExpression with $type number/string, which must not be sparse). Rust must declare the same IndexModels by name/keys/options for all ~70 documents, or the old ones are dropped or duplicated. Best approach: one idempotent `ensure_indexes()` module that copies each model's list, keeping Mongo's default names (field_1_field2_-1). Indexes in this area: users {email:1 unique}, {github_id:1 unique partial $type number}; sessions {refresh_token_hash:1 unique}, {user_id:1,last_used_at:-1}; site_users {username:1 unique}, {discord_id:1 unique partial number}, {claimed_trove_name:1 unique partial string}, {creator_token_hash:1 unique partial string}; site_sessions {refresh_token_hash:1 unique}, {site_user_id:1,last_used_at:-1}; username_change_requests {status:1,created_at:-1}, {site_user_id:1,created_at:-1}; api_tokens {hashed_token:1 unique}, {user_id:1}, {revoked:1,last_used_at:1}, {revoked:1,expires_at:1}; usage_events {user_id:1,created_at:-1}, {token_id:1,created_at:-1}, {status_code:1,created_at:-1}; email_outbox {status:1,next_attempt_at:1}; runtime_config {key:1 unique}. _ensure_ttl_index: try create; on OperationFailure drop any single-field index on that field and recreate. Never use collMod: the app's Mongo user only has readWrite (mongo-init.js). Datetimes: BSON dates are ms precision and read back tz-aware UTC. Beanie writes optional fields as explicit null (that is why indexes are partial, not sparse), _id is an ObjectId, and there is no revision_id or class_id. Rust structs must serialize None as null, not skip it, or partial-index and $exists-based queries break. Pydantic responses render a round-tripped datetime as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmm000Z' (6 fractional digits when nonzero, none when zero), while a just-created in-memory object has full microsecond precision. upsert_by(model, key, value, fields, stamp) is a find_one then insert-or-save helper used by the relay refreshers. Pagination: cursor = str(ObjectId) of the last row, newest first by _id desc, query _id < cursor, fetch limit+1; a bad cursor gives 400 'Invalid cursor'; Page{items,next_cursor,has_more}. paginate() is an offset count+skip+limit. Postgres pool: 2..10 per worker (multiply by worker count today), a jsonb text codec, and the schema ensured at boot (other areas own the DDL).

components.name: Dev-portal accounts (email/password, sessions, GitHub OAuth, GDPR)
data: Mongo users, sessions, api_tokens, usage_events (export/delete), email_outbox (via queue_email)
Redis: oauthstate:{state} '1' EX 600; oauthx:{code} JSON {"a":access,"r":refresh} EX 120 (GETDEL on exchange); rl:signup|login|resend|forgot:{ip}; loginfail/loginlock
Outbound: github.com/login/oauth/access_token, api.github.com/user, /user/emails; HIBP; captcha
python_deps: email-validator (pydantic EmailStr) -> email_address crate or a port (special-use TLDs like .test/.local/.localhost/.invalid rejected; domain normalized)
background: FastAPI BackgroundTasks after the response: verification, new-login, password-changed, email-change, reset, token mails (all just insert into email_outbox)
components.port_notes: Response models in field order. UserPublic {id,email,display_name,is_active,is_verified,is_superuser,roles,created_at,last_login_at}; TokenResponse {access_token,refresh_token,token_type:'bearer',expires_in:900}; SessionPublic {id,device,created_at,last_used_at,expires_at,current}; MessageResponse {message}. Datetimes use pydantic 'Z' format. Signup: rate limit signup:{ip}, captcha (400 captcha_failed), lowercase email, disposable blocklist (400 disposable_email), exists gives 409 email_taken, HIBP, argon2 hash, insert, background verify mail; returns 201 UserPublic. Request bodies: password min_length=settings.password_min_length (8) max 256; display_name max 80. Login order: rate limit login:{ip}, then captcha, then lockout (429 account_locked + Retry-After), then lookup/verify (401 invalid_credentials 'Incorrect email or password' and record_failure), then clear lockout, then require_verified_for_login (403 email_unverified), then the new-device check (Session with the same device label), then last_login_at, then issue_tokens (Session doc: refresh = token_urlsafe(48), stored sha256 hex, expires +30d, device label). Refresh rotates the refresh hash, updates last_used_at/device, and mints access with sid; invalid gives 401 not_authenticated. Logout is idempotent and returns 204. logout-all/change-password/verify-email-change/reset-password call revoke_all_sessions (token_version += 1, then a mass revoked=true update). Change-password returns NEW tokens. Purpose tokens (same HS256 key): email_verify {sub,type,iat,exp +48h}; password_reset adds fp = sha256(hashed_password)[:16] (+1h, single-use because the hash changes); email_change adds new=<email> and fp = sha256(current email)[:16] (+48h). Links: {api_url}/auth/verify-email?token=, /auth/reset-password?token=, /auth/verify-email-change?token=. The GET HTML pages use the _html_page template (escaped title, inline style; the reset form has an inline script that POSTs JSON; the API CSP allows inline script). Status codes: verify failure 400, email-change conflict 409. GDPR export: jsonable_encoder (datetimes '+00:00', NOT 'Z'), Content-Disposition attachment; filename="kiwi-export.json". delete-account (confirm_email must match) hard-deletes api_tokens, sessions and usage_events, then the user, and returns 204. GitHub OAuth: requires Redis (else 307 to {dev_url}/#oauth_error=unavailable); start returns 307 to the authorize URL with client_id, redirect_uri={api_url}/auth/oauth/github/callback, scope 'read:user user:email', state, allow_signup=true, in that param order. The callback consumes state via DEL (0 means oauth_error=state), exchanges the code, picks the primary+verified email else any verified, find-or-creates (link by github_id, else by email and set is_verified/clear bounced plus a notice mail, else create with a random unusable password), issues tokens, stores oauthx, and returns 307 {dev_url}/#oauth=<code>. Errors are 307 #oauth_error=missing|state|exchange|github|noemail|inactive. Exchange uses GETDEL; a bad code is 400 bad_request. Disposable list: copy the frozenset of 69 domains.

components.name: API tokens management + token-use accounting
data: Mongo api_tokens {user_id, name, prefix, hashed_token, scopes(int), ip_salt, allowed_ip_hashes[], revoked, revoked_at, revoke_reason, expires_at, expiry_warned, created_at, last_used_at, rotated_at, request_count}
Mongo usage_events (aggregations)
Redis: tok:pending:{token_id}, tok:gate:{token_id} (debounce Lua), rl:tokencreate:{user_id}
components.port_notes: Everything is session-JWT (dev portal) auth. TokenPublic field order: id, name, prefix, scopes, scope_names, allowed_ip_count, revoked, revoked_at, revoke_reason, created_at, last_used_at, rotated_at, expires_at, request_count. TokenCreatedResponse is the same plus a trailing token (the secret, shown once). Create: require_verified_for_tokens (403 email_unverified), rate limit tokencreate:{user_id} with token_creation_daily_limit per 86400, is_valid_mask (400), salt = token_urlsafe(16) always minted, allowed_ips are normalized/deduped/HMAC'd (400 'Invalid IP: x', or the CIDR message), expires_in_days in {30,60,90,null} (default 30), 201. CreateTokenRequest: name 1..80, scopes int >= 0, allowed_ips list. Edit: name and/or allowed_ips (a full replace; [] clears); revoked gives 400 'Token is revoked'. Rotate: new secret/prefix, rotated_at=now, last_used_at=None, expiry_warned=False, keeps the id/scopes/IPs/expiry; returns 200 TokenCreatedResponse. Revoke: reason 1..200, idempotent, returns TokenPublic. A foreign or missing token gives 404 'Token not found'; a malformed ObjectId path param gives 422 (FastAPI). Activity: days 1..365 (default 7) and ActivitySummary {window_days,total_requests,error_count,rate_limited,avg_duration_ms,by_day[{date 'YYYY-MM-DD' UTC,count,error_count,avg_duration_ms}],by_endpoint[{route,method,count,error_count,avg_duration_ms}]}. Three Mongo aggregations (error = status>=400, rate_limited = status==429, avg rounded to 2 dp with Python round-half-even on binary floats). by_day is sorted by _id asc; by_endpoint is sorted by count desc only, so tie order is unstable. Token-use debounce Lua (copy exactly): n=INCR pending; if SET gate '1' NX EX interval then SET pending '0', EXPIRE pending interval*4, return n; else return -1. delta>0 does $inc request_count by delta and $set last_used_at=now. Without Redis, or on a Redis error, write each request directly (delta 1). The client IP is deliberately NOT stored.

components.name: Site accounts (Discord-only sign-in, cookies, profile, claims, GDPR anonymize)
data: Mongo site_users, site_sessions, username_change_requests

Mongo (export/anonymize): mod_projects, modpack_projects, mod_profiles, mod_stars, modpack_stars, giveaway_entries, giveaways, dm_subscriptions, site_webhooks, image_designs, mod_git_tokens, mod_claim_requests, email_outbox (exact names from those features' Beanie Settings)

Redis: site_oauthstate:{state} JSON {"mode":"web|app","next":path} EX 600 (legacy plain-string value accepted); site_oauthx:{code} JSON {"a","r"} EX 120 (GETDEL); site_discord_tok:{site_user_id} = Discord access token EX clamp(expires_in, 60, 7d)
Postgres (indirect): app.trove.leaderboards.service.player_history / player_history_series for the claim baseline + trove-stats
Outbound: discord.com/api/oauth2/token, /api/users/@me, /api/users/@me/guilds
python_deps: starlette set_cookie/delete_cookie -> axum-extra cookie / cookie crate
components.port_notes: Foundation-critical: get_current_site_user / get_optional_site_user / get_current_verified_site_user are used by mods hub, modpacks, giveaways, webhooks, DM subs, images, bot dashboard, etc. Credential order: Bearer first; else the kiwi_site_access cookie, accepted ONLY if Origin is in {scheme://netloc of app_url, of api_url} (+ http://localhost:8913 and 127.0.0.1:8913 when debug), or if there is no Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site == 'same-origin'. The JWT must have kind=='site' and ver==SiteUser.token_version with is_active. The optional variant swallows every error as anonymous. The verified variant gives 403 email_unverified "Your account isn't verified yet.". Site access JWT = the dev claims + kind:'site'. Cookies (Starlette format; attribute order is cosmetic, but Domain/Path must match to clear): kiwi_site_access=<jwt> (HttpOnly, Path=/, Max-Age 900); kiwi_site_refresh=<refresh> (HttpOnly, Path=/v1/site-auth, Max-Age 2592000); kiwi_site_session=1 (NOT HttpOnly, Path=/, Max-Age 2592000). All SameSite=lax, Secure when app_url is https, Domain='.'+last two labels of the app_url host when it has 3+ labels (.aallyn.net), else host-only. delete_cookie mirrors the attributes with Max-Age=0 and the 1970 expires. Refresh/logout take the body token, else the refresh cookie. A failed refresh gives 401 with cookies NOT cleared. Success sets all three cookies and returns SiteTokenResponse {access_token,refresh_token,token_type,expires_in}. Logout/logout-all clear the cookies and return 204. SiteUserPublic order: id, username, discord_handle (falls back to username), notify_email, display_name, avatar_url, is_active, is_verified, claimed_trove_name, claimed_trove_display, claimed_at, claim_verified, claim_verified_at, claim_baseline_board_count, created_at, last_login_at. avatar_url = https://cdn.discordapp.com/avatars/{id}/{hash}.{gif if hash starts 'a_' else png}?size=128, else /embed/avatars/{(id>>22)%6}.png, else null. PATCH /me: display_name stripped ('' becomes null); notify_email '' clears it, otherwise EmailStr-validated and lowercased, else 400 "That doesn't look like a valid email address.". Claim: name stripped; lowercase must be unique among other users or 409 with code 'bad_request'. The baseline is the best score per board uuid (str keys) from leaderboard player_history(limit=500). verify-trove-claim always reports pending unless the master approved. trove-stats returns {claimed:false,items:[],series:null} or {claimed,player_name,items,series}. GET /sessions returns a plain list of {id,device,created_at,last_used_at,expires_at} using iso() ('+00:00' format, NO 'current' flag), in natural order. Username-request DTO {id,site_user_id,current_username,requested_username,status,reason,created_at,resolved_at} with iso() datetimes, wrapped as {"request":..|null}; delete returns {"ok":true}. Username rules: ^[a-z0-9_.]{3,24}$, no leading '.', no '..', 20 reserved words (409 with code bad_request). Discord start: client=app selects app mode; next is sanitized (backslashes become '/', scheme/netloc dropped, path must start with '/'). Without Redis, emit an error. Otherwise 307 to https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id&redirect_uri={api_url}/v1/site-auth/oauth/discord/callback&response_type=code&scope=identify+guilds&state. Callback: consume state with GETDEL (bad gives _back #oauth_error=state); POST the token with form grant_type=authorization_code; GET @me; find by discord_id (sync avatar + live handle; the frozen username is never touched) or create (username from _unique_username: strip to [a-z0-9_.], collapse dots, lstrip '.', [:20], pad with 'kiwi' if under 3 chars, collision suffix token_hex(2), 12 tries, fallback 'kiwi'+hex16); then store the Discord token, issue tokens, and set site_oauthx. Web mode gives 307 {app_url}/login[?next=quote(path, safe='/')]#discord=<code> or #oauth_error=<e>. App mode returns an HTML interstitial that runs location.replace('btt://auth/discord?code=..'). Exchange: GETDEL, set cookies, return tokens. Export: jsonable_encoder ('+00:00'), filename better-trove-tools-export.json. Delete (confirm_username) anonymizes in place: purge outbox mail to notify_email; delete sessions, git tokens, profile, claim requests, username requests, DM subs, webhooks and image designs; decrement star/entry counters then delete stars/entries; set the anonymized handle 'deleted_'+hex16 on giveaways.winner_username and on mod/modpack owner_username/owner_handle; strip the user from collaborators; wipe the user row (is_active=false, is_deleted=true, token_version+1); clear the Discord token. Return 204. Admin approve/reject/set-username helpers live here and are used by the admin area.

components.name: Usage metrics (middleware, buffered recorder, aggregations)
data: Mongo usage_events {user_id, token_id, method, route (template), path, status_code, duration_ms(float, 2dp), created_at}; TTL created_at_ttl = usage_retention_days*86400 (30)
python_deps: asyncio buffer + insert_many -> tokio mpsc + interval + mongodb insert_many
background: BufferedRecorder loop per worker: flush every 3.0s or as soon as 200 are buffered; hard cap 10,000 (drops the oldest with a warning); drained on shutdown; before start(), record() does fire-and-forget single inserts
components.port_notes: Recorded only when an API-token dependency ran (request.state.usage_token_id set), including requests that then got 403 ip_not_allowed or 429. Session-JWT and anonymous calls are never recorded. route = the matched route TEMPLATE in FastAPI syntax, e.g. /v1/updates/{branch}/file/{path:path}. axum 0.8 MatchedPath gives '{*path}' for wildcards, so map it back to the FastAPI spelling or historical per-endpoint stats split. Falls back to the concrete path when there is no route. duration_ms = round(perf_counter delta*1000, 2), measured from when the usage middleware starts (inside idempotency/security), so it includes handler time only. HEAD requests are recorded with method HEAD. aggregate_activity is shared with the admin area (see the token component for output shape and order). Best-effort: a crash loses the last unflushed batch.

components.name: Email outbox, SMTP mailer, HTML template
data: Mongo email_outbox {to, subject, text, html, status pending|sending|sent|bounced|failed, attempts, last_error(<=500 chars), next_attempt_at, claimed_at, created_at, sent_at}; index {status:1,next_attempt_at:1}; TTL created_at_ttl 30d
Mongo users (email_bounced flag lookup/set)
SMTP: smtp_host:smtp_port (prod Postfix via host.docker.internal:25), optional STARTTLS/implicit TLS/auth
python_deps: aiosmtplib + email.message.EmailMessage -> lettre (tokio1, rustls) with a multipart/alternative builder
background: Email worker per uvicorn worker: claim up to 50 messages back to back, then sleep email_worker_poll_seconds (10)
components.port_notes:
queue_email is a no-op (logged) when SMTP is unset, and skips addresses whose User has email_bounced=true (matched on the lowercased to). Claim = find_one_and_update {$or:[{status:pending,next_attempt_at<=now},{status:sending,claimed_at<=now-5min}]} -> {$set status:sending, claimed_at:now}, sorted by next_attempt_at asc, returning AFTER. This is safe with multiple consumers. Success: status sent, sent_at, attempts+1. Failure: attempts+1; permanent (SMTPRecipientsRefused, or a 5xx reply) gives status bounced and flags User.email_bounced. attempts >= email_max_attempts (5) gives failed. Otherwise pending with next_attempt_at = now + 60*2^(attempts-1) s. Message: From '{mail_from_name} <{mail_from}>' (Kiwi <no-reply@aallyn.net>), To, Subject, Date (formatdate localtime), Message-ID make_msgid(domain=mail_from domain), text/plain body plus an optional text/html alternative (Python EmailMessage set_content/add_alternative gives multipart/alternative, utf-8, 7bit/quoted-printable chosen automatically). 15s timeout. The HTML template _BASE (branded table layout; app_name, heading, paragraphs, optional button {label,url}, optional note, footer dev_url/docs_url) is rendered with autoescape; copy it verbatim into minijinja. The plain text is the paragraphs joined by blank lines + '

{label}: {url}' + '

{note}'. Other areas (giveaways, moderation, notify_email) also queue through this.

data: Redis lists: kiwi:webhooks:queue, kiwi:dmsubs:queue (LPUSH JSON default=str / BRPOP 5s); pub/sub channel kiwi:events (events area)

LoopTask / RedisListConsumer / PeriodicRefresher are the scaffolds used by giveaways, webhooks, DM subs, news, feeds, events, chaos, delves, btt_releases, mod_stats, steam_workshop
components.port_notes: Provide generic Rust equivalents. PeriodicRefresher(refresh, name, delay = const or closure re-evaluated each cycle; log the result and swallow errors). RedisListConsumer: BRPOP queue 5s timeout; a JSON-decoded item goes to the handler; errors are logged and the loop continues; it is a no-op when Redis is unset. enqueue_or_inline(payload): requires payload.type in deliverable_types and the feature flag on; LPUSH json.dumps(payload, default=str), or without Redis spawn delivery inline. Per-worker today, so N workers mean N BRPOP consumers (still exactly-once per job). The maintenance sweep runs on every worker's boot (12 times). warn_expiring_tokens can double-send under that race; the digest is guarded by the system_state marker (still racy). A single Rust scheduler fixes both. delivery_health.record_delivery: ok resets consecutive_failures/last_error and stamps last_delivered_at; a status in permanent_statuses gives active=false + disabled_reason; otherwise failures+1 and auto-disable at 12; updated_at is always set. discord_fmt: '<t:{int}:{style}>' and unix_to_iso via datetime.isoformat ('+00:00'). bootstrap_admin: when ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD are both set, create (display_name 'Administrator', superuser, verified) or promote, and reset the password hash if it doesn't verify (env is authoritative). internal_get never raises (returns None on failure).

components.name: GitHub secret-scanning partner webhook
data: Mongo api_tokens (revoke), users (notify)
Outbound: settings.github_secret_scanning_keys_url (https://api.github.com/meta/public_keys/secret_scanning), keys cached in-process, refetched when the key id is unknown
python_deps: cryptography ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 DER verify -> p256 + ecdsa (Signature::from_der) + pem/spki parsing
background: BackgroundTasks: send_token_compromised_email after the response
components.port_notes: Reads the RAW body (it must not be re-serialized before verification). Headers Github-Public-Key-Identifier / Github-Public-Key-Signature (base64 DER). Verification failure gives 401 not_authenticated 'Invalid or missing secret-scanning signature' (skipped when github_secret_scanning_verify=false). Non-JSON gives 400 'Body must be JSON'; non-array gives 400 'Body must be a JSON array of token matches'. Each entry with a truthy token produces {"token_raw":token,"token_type":type or 'kiwi_api_token',"label":"true_positive"|"false_positive"} in input order; non-dicts and empty tokens are skipped. A failed checksum, or no hashed_token match, is false_positive. A match is revoked (reason 'Exposed publicly (detected by secret scanning)') if not already revoked, and is true_positive either way. Response 200 JSON list.

components.port_notes: One image (trove-app:latest, target app) runs api, web and bot with different commands; builder is a second stage adding SteamCMD (i386). Ports: api container :8000 -> ${BIND_ADDR:-127.0.0.1}:15546 (api.aallyn.net and the old dev hostnames; the edge proxy forwards everything and the app 301s pages to trove.); web :8000 -> :15547 (trove.aallyn.net, no DB, talks to http://api:8000 with X-Internal-Key); portal nginx :80 -> :25470 (dev.aallyn.net SPA, static ./portal/html); docs nginx :80 -> :25468 (docs.aallyn.net, static ./docs, proxies /openapi.json from the api); mongo 127.0.0.1:27016->27017; postgres 127.0.0.1:5432; redis internal only. uvicorn runs with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips ${FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS:-127.0.0.1}, and the Rust server must implement the same trusted-proxy X-Forwarded-For/-Proto rewrite (rate-limit keys, IP-allowlist HMACs and scheme depend on it). mem_limit api 2g, web 512m, bot 512m. deploy.sh: git pull --ff-only (fatal on failure), minify site/static via a tools venv (refuse to deploy without *.min.js/*.min.css), chmod portal/docs, `docker compose up -d --remove-orphans --build`, force-recreate portal+docs, prune dangling images and cap the builder cache at 10GB. It does not pass -f docker-compose.prod.yml, so the prod overlay applies only through COMPOSE_FILE in the server .env (verify on the box). Things that cannot become Rust and stay subprocess or sidecar: the JPEXS FFDec Java decompiler (spawn `java -Xmx768m -jar /opt/ffdec/ffdec.jar` with the same timeouts and 2-concurrency semaphore), SteamCMD and the Apache Flex SDK in the builder, the discord.py gateway bot (portable to serenity but a separate effort), RapidOCR (portable via ort with the same det/cls/rec ONNX models but pre/post-processing must be reimplemented exactly), plus fonts as system files for any text rendering. The Rust multi-stage build replaces the maturin wheel stage with `cargo build --release` of the server binary; the app stage still needs the JRE, fonts, git and libgl (only if OCR stays on onnxruntime C++).

Shared low-level conventions every area relies on: APIError/ErrorCode envelope, request-id task-local, require_scope/public_scope/require_master_ingest/get_current_user/get_current_superuser/get_current_site_user/get_optional_site_user dependencies, check_rate_limit, get_redis/get_db/postgres acquire, utcnow/iso/to_oid/client_ip/device_label helpers, PeriodicRefresher/LoopTask/RedisListConsumer/enqueue_or_inline, BufferedRecorder, queue_email/render_email, Page/paginate_newest_first, upsert_by
hardest_parts: /openapi.json parity: FastAPI generates the spec from pydantic models across hundreds of routes, then main.py post-processes it (🔓 tokenless and ⭐ master markers, optional-security [{}] entries, an APIToken scheme note) and prunes it per request from live feature flags. The Redoc docs site consumes it. Rust needs utoipa schemas that mirror every model, or a frozen exported spec plus a (path, method) -> flag pruning table

JSON byte-parity across serializers: pydantic response_model datetimes render as '...T..:..:..Z', or '.ffffffZ' when microseconds are nonzero (Mongo round-trips are ms precision, giving .123000Z). jsonable_encoder/iso()/isoformat paths (GDPR exports, site sessions, username DTOs, discord_fmt) render '+00:00'. Python float repr ('1e+16', '1e-05') differs from ryu/serde_json ('1e16', '1e-5'). Also compact separators, ensure_ascii=False, model field order, explicit nulls, and round-half-even 2dp averages

422 validation errors: FastAPI emits pydantic v2 error lists (type/loc/msg/input/ctx) for bad bodies, query params, path ObjectIds and malformed JSON. axum/serde rejections must be remapped into the same envelope and status, and details will only be approximate

Middleware header semantics: setdefault-vs-overwrite rules, credential-triggered 'private, no-store' + Vary merge, the 413 that skips security headers, the api-host 301 outside security, Starlette CORS preflight ('OK' 200 text / 400 'Disallowed CORS origin', Max-Age 600, echoed headers), the outer public-asset wildcard CORS override, gzip-only-when-beneficial with exact Content-Length and no Vary on uncompressed bodies, HEAD handling that must not open SSE streams, and X-RateLimit-* headers currently present only on endpoints that return models rather than Response objects

Auth artifact interoperability during a mixed cutover: argon2-cffi PHC params (m=65536,t=3,p=4) vs the Rust crate's defaults; PyJWT HS256 with zero leeway and future-iat rejection vs jsonwebtoken's 60s default leeway; the API token format with a nonstandard base62 alphabet (a-zA-Z0-9) and CRC32 checksum; sha256 refresh/token hashes; HMAC IP hashes over Python-normalized IP strings; pydantic EmailStr acceptance rules

Mongo bootstrap: re-declaring ~70 Beanie models' indexes (partial unique on $type, never sparse, because Beanie writes explicit nulls), TTL-index drop/recreate without collMod (the app user is readWrite only), one-time index drops/backfills, and preserving explicit-null field writes that queries and partial indexes depend on

Going from N uvicorn workers (12 in .env) to one tokio process: every lifespan loop and in-process cache (runtime_config 5s, GitHub keys, rate-limit member sequence) is per-worker today. Races like duplicate expiry-warning mails disappear, but anything that implicitly relied on per-worker fan-out (SSE bus subscriber per worker, Postgres pool sizing 2..10 x N) must be re-sized deliberately

Keeping Redis key and Lua script compatibility (rl:*, idem:*, tok:pending/gate, loginfail/loginlock, oauthstate/oauthx, site_oauthstate/site_oauthx, site_discord_tok, kiwi:webhooks:queue, kiwi:dmsubs:queue) so Python and Rust can run side by side and share budgets and state

Non-Rust runtimes stuck behind the core image: JPEXS FFDec (Java subprocess), RapidOCR/onnxruntime (port to the ort crate with identical pre/post-processing or keep a sidecar), the discord.py gateway bot, and SteamCMD/Flex SDK in the builder

summary: This area holds three domains. Leaderboards is the largest, at about 10k Python lines plus about 1.6k of route/site/schema code. It ingests about 700k-row LeaderBot.cfg dumps into partitioned Postgres (entry is partitioned by trove-day, about 1.5B rows, with a cold tablespace). It serves read APIs from a Redis snapshot cache that is gated by a published 'ready anchor'. It runs a heavy background warmer every ~30 min and after each ingest: cheater/alt-cluster detection, player activity, class activity, renames, duplicates, cache warm and cold-tiering. It also has several hour-long replay or backfill jobs. Market (about 1.7k lines) keeps listings in Postgres market_listing and its allow-list and categories in Mongo, and serves listing/analytics SQL plus a pure-CPU anomaly scan. Store (about 0.9k lines) is a Mongo-only catalog with price history and availability intervals. kiwi_native already covers the hot CPU kernels: dump parse, binary-COPY decode, activity pair/class sets, duplicate grouping, aggregate replay, rename fingerprints and detection families/history. Nothing here needs a non-Rust runtime. The port is mostly SQL plus large amounts of exact-semantics Python logic: detection, rounding, float formatting, and the split between /v1 pydantic shapes and raw /site dict shapes.

components.port_notes: Parse: lines `name_id$category_id$uuid = name$category##rank;player;score|...`. A contest overlay category (Leaderboard_Category_Contests[_Daily]) folds into a per-dump contest flag instead of becoming a board. The real-category line wins (first seen). FAVORITES is dropped. Board order is first-seen. Entries: chunk.strip() uses Python isspace; exactly 3 ';' parts; rank must pass str.isdecimal (Unicode digits allowed, int() of them); score uses Python float() grammar (whitespace, '_', inf/nan, Unicode digits). kiwi-core lbdump returns None in those cases. A full port must implement the Python fallback itself. The upload is decoded as UTF-8 strict, else errors='replace' (from_utf8_lossy matches). insert_dump: normalize_timestamp zeroes seconds, rejects anything >5 min in the future or >14 days old unless backfill (-1), and aliases 00:00 UTC to 11:00. An out-of-range client ts falls back to _trove_day_anchor() (latest 11:00 UTC) and summary.rejected_timestamp is set. The completeness guard (runtime capture_*) compares {board: count} with the previous anchor. Across a daily/weekly reset only boards whose override is 'none' are judged. A rejected dump returns {skipped:true, reason, missing_boards, collapsed_boards, prev_anchor, prev_boards, cur_boards} and is still backlog-saved. write_snapshot runs in ONE transaction: ensure_partition, `DELETE FROM entry WHERE anchor=$1` (count parsed from the 'DELETE n' tag), board upsert, contest insert, CREATE TEMP _stg, binary COPY, `ANALYZE _stg`, `INSERT INTO player(name,name_lower) SELECT min(name COLLATE "C"), lower(name) COLLATE "C" FROM _stg GROUP BY lower(name) COLLATE "C" ON CONFLICT(name_lower) DO UPDATE SET name=EXCLUDED.name WHERE player.name IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.name`, `INSERT INTO entry SELECT s.board_uuid,s.anchor,s.rank,s.score,p.id FROM _stg s JOIN player p ON p.name_lower=lower(s.name)` (Postgres lower(), not Rust lower), the case-collision upsert into player_duplicate (kind case/both merge rules), then the agg fold (DISTINCT ON(player_id,board_uuid) ORDER BY rank ASC, score DESC; LEAST/GREATEST; appearances +1 only if anchor > last_folded_anchor; last_rise rule `CASE WHEN EXCLUDED.last_seen > a.last_seen AND EXCLUDED.latest_score > a.latest_score THEN EXCLUDED.last_seen ELSE a.last_rise END`). Summary dict: {boards, entries, created_at, cleared_before_insert, archived_old:0}. After a successful ingest: invalidate_anchor in Redis, backlog.save, events publish('leaderboard', str(anchor), {anchor,boards,entries}), trigger_warmer unless backfill/warm=false. Response LeaderboardInsertResponse {accepted, bytes, message} with exact message strings. Status 202 normally, response.status_code=200 for sync. Schema DDL runs at startup (IF NOT EXISTS plus ALTER ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS). Trove day = 11:00 UTC boundary, computed as ((a-39600)//86400)*86400+39600 (floor division also for negatives). The pool uses command_timeout=120s.
already_native: kiwi_native.lb_parse (kiwi-core lbdump::parse) for dump parsing; Python fallback for Unicode digits/odd floats/lone surrogates

components.port_notes: Read SQL to reproduce verbatim. (1) list_timestamps uses a recursive loose index scan `WITH RECURSIVE a AS (SELECT (SELECT max(anchor) FROM entry [WHERE anchor>=$2]) UNION ALL SELECT (SELECT max(e.anchor) FROM entry e WHERE e.anchor<a.anchor [AND e.anchor>=$2]) FROM a WHERE a.anchor IS NOT NULL) SELECT anchor FROM a WHERE anchor IS NOT NULL LIMIT $1`. Never use DISTINCT; it times out on the cold tier. (2) list_days uses the same pattern jumping per trove-day: `e.anchor < ((d.anchor-$2)/86400)*86400+$2` with $2=39600. (3) list_boards_at: `SELECT b.*, bc.type AS contest_type FROM (SELECT DISTINCT board_uuid FROM entry WHERE anchor=$1) e JOIN board b ... LEFT JOIN board_contest bc ON bc.board_uuid=b.uuid AND bc.anchor=$1 ORDER BY b.category, b.name`. The order depends on the DB collation, so keep it in SQL. (4) get_board plus contests ORDER BY anchor. (5) list_entries: count(*) then `SELECT p.name AS player_name,e.rank,e.score FROM entry e JOIN player p ... WHERE board_uuid=$1 AND anchor=$2 ORDER BY e.rank LIMIT $3 OFFSET $4`. (6) previous_day_anchor: `MAX(anchor) WHERE board_uuid=$1 AND anchor<trove_day_start`. (7) prev_rows_for_players by p.name_lower=ANY($3), keyed by Python name.lower(). (8) top_entries_for_boards: unnest($1::int[]) CROSS JOIN LATERAL(... ORDER BY e.rank, e.player_id LIMIT 1) JOIN player. (9) player_rows and player_rows_window resolve the player id first (`name_lower=lower($1)` with name.strip()), then `entry WHERE player_id=$1 AND NOT(board_uuid=ANY($2::int[]))`, an optional anchor window, `ORDER BY anchor DESC LIMIT`. Non-player boards are {1100, 21012}. (10) player_board_summary reads player_board_agg JOIN player `ORDER BY a.best_rank ASC, a.last_seen DESC`. (11) player_last_played: max(last_rise) excluding the last_played_excluded_board_uuids CSV. (12) board_top_series: DISTINCT anchors >= window, top-N at latest by rank, series by player_id=ANY. (13) board_meta/board_kinds/board_reset_kind: effective reset_kind = valid override in {daily,weekly,none}, else the hardcoded daily {32000} / weekly set, else 'default'. (14) search_players: a prefix UNION ALL contains pass on name_lower LIKE with ESCAPE '\\', EXISTS player_board_agg on a non-club board, ORDER BY tier, length(name_lower), name_lower. total = len(names). Wire traps: /v1 routes serialize through pydantic models, so fields are reordered and filtered and ints in float fields become floats ('5.0'). /site routes JSONResponse the raw dict in insertion order with compact separators and ensure_ascii=False. Examples: /v1 LeaderboardInfo drops reset_kind_override. /v1 entries always carry prev_*/rank_delta/score_delta (null) and is_new:false, while /site items carry delta keys only when comparable (order player_name,rank,score,is_new,prev_rank,prev_score,rank_delta,score_delta). /v1 profile drops renames, alt_clusters, duplicate, boards[].board_name_id and recent[].slot/slots. /v1 series drops duplicate_boards and slot/slots. History points carry synthetic reset-zero pairs at R-1 (pre-reset score/rank) and R (0, 0.0). The weekly reset is Monday 11:00 UTC. Validation: /v1 created_at goes through normalize_timestamp (400 'created_at must align to a Trove reset ...' when -1), so /v1 can only read the last 14 days. /site boards/entries return 403 envelope 'Captures older than N days aren't available.' (leaderboards_anon_retention_days). /v1/{uuid:int} uses Starlette's int convertor (digits only; a non-int segment is a 404, not a 422). /site/{uuid} non-int gives a 422 envelope. Player name path params are percent-decoded before routing in Starlette (%2F breaks routing). Archive bucket: when anchor < now - leaderboards_archive_query_threshold_days, check rl:lb_archive:{token.id} and emit X-RateLimit-Archive-Limit/Remaining/Reset. Board history and series charge using now-days*86400 before the cache read. Player series clamps days to hot_window_days. hot_window_start = trove_day_start(now) - (max(1,tier_after_days)-1)*86400. Cache-Control: records 'public, max-age=900'; /site config 15, timestamps 30, days 120, boards 60, entries/players/profile/series 30, {uuid}/history and health 60, records 900, board-icon 604800 (image/png, name must match ^[a-z0-9_]+$). Python round() is banker's rounding (mastery_records int(round(score)), sigil round). Health metrics use round(x,4)/round(x,2). Gini/median are hand-rolled. mastery points_to_mr/mr_to_points is a byte-exact RTT port capped at level 1001; Geode is capped at 100 with uncapped_level/capped. Profile also needs trove.stats class tables (pr 1000+i, effort 4000+i, paragon 5000+i) and runs 8 lookups concurrently, each one never-raise.
depends_on: auth require_scope/public_scope, rate limiter, runtime_config, error envelope

data: Redis lb:cache:timestamps (list of up to 365 anchors, EX 6h)
Redis lb:cache:days (EX 12h)
Redis lb:cache:boards:{anchor} (EX 6h)
Redis lb:cache:entries:{anchor}:{uuid}:{offset}:{limit} ({items,total,comparison}, EX 6h)
Redis lb:cache:bhist:{uuid}:{days}:{top} (EX hot_retention_days*86400)
Redis lb:cache:ready_anchor (bare int JSON, EX retention seconds)
Redis lb:cache:cheaters:{anchor}, lb:cache:activity:{anchor} (EX retention seconds)
Redis lb:cache:activity_series:{period}, lb:cache:activity_class_series:{period}, lb:cache:activity_class_current (EX 300)
PG reads via service/pg_store; cold-tier ALTERs (see maintenance)
python_deps: redis.asyncio (get/set ex, scan_iter, delete) -> fred or redis-rs ConnectionManager (SCAN cursor loop)
background: leaderboards-warmer task in EVERY uvicorn worker (8 in prod), no cross-worker lock. Starts 2s after boot. The first pass is skipped if the published anchor's persisted cheaters pass is younger than cheaters_cache_ttl_seconds and no newer anchor exists. Each iteration runs sequentially: detect_possible_cheaters(force) -> activity.estimate_active_players(force) -> class_activity.estimate_class_activity(force) -> renames.detect_latest -> duplicates.detect_latest (each non-fatal) -> cache.warm() -> set_ready_anchor(detection anchor, else latest) -> warm_board_histories (7d/top5 for every board, concurrency 6) -> warm_days (only when the trove-day rolled over) -> cold-tier at most once/24h with 3 partitions per pass. Sleep = max(30, ttl - elapsed - resumed_age), ttl=cheaters_cache_ttl_seconds (default 1800), re-read each loop. trigger_warmer() (ingest/recompute/admin) wakes only the local worker's Event.
components.port_notes: Values are Python json.dumps (default ', ' and ': ' separators). Any JSON reader works, but if Python and Rust share Redis during migration, keep key names, TTLs and payload shapes identical (e.g. entries cache {items,total,comparison}; a missing comparison defaults to {comparable:false, prev_anchor:null, reason:'no_prior_snapshot'}). get_timestamps returns the cached list (miss: list_timestamps(365), then cache) capped to <= ready_anchor when one exists, then sliced. get_ready_anchor accepts only an int. cache.warm(): rewrites timestamps, then for the latest anchor of each of the last hot_retention_days trove-days caches boards and the first board's first page (limit 100, offset 0). invalidate_anchor deletes boards:{a}, cheaters:{a}, activity:{a} and SCANs entries:{a}:*. invalidate_views deletes timestamps, ready_anchor, boards:*, entries:*, bhist:*. invalidate_all_activity SCANs lb:cache:activity* (also catches class keys). invalidate_cheaters SCANs cheaters:*. reset_all SCANs lb:cache:*. Every cache op is best-effort and swallows exceptions. Without Redis everything degrades to direct PG reads and get_ready_anchor=None (fail-open). views/recompute returns {recomputed, keys_cleared, anchor, board_charts_warmed} with status 200; warm returns {warming:true} with 202. A Rust single-process server should run ONE warmer (a Redis lock is recommended if multiple replicas). In-process caches (detection _CACHE/_LAST_GOOD/_COMOVEMENT_CACHE, activity _CACHE/_LAST_GOOD, renames scan guard) were per-worker in Python.
depends_on: detection, activity, class_activity, renames, duplicates compute

files: app/trove/leaderboards/detection.py (compute pipeline, checks, clusters, co-movement, schedule, fusion, confidence, format)
data: PG entry/player via entries_by_board_at (`SELECT e.board_uuid,p.name,e.rank,e.score FROM entry e JOIN player p ... WHERE e.anchor=$1 [AND board_uuid=ANY($2)] ORDER BY e.board_uuid,e.rank`)

Redis lb:cache:cheaters:{anchor}, lb:cache:ready_anchor
python_deps: re (_STEM_SUFFIX_RE, Unicode \s/\d) + str.translate leet map + str.lower -> regex crate with Unicode classes / hand-rolled (kiwi-core detection::name_stem covers ASCII only)
background: Computed only by the warmer (force=True). Serving path: in-process cache keyed by (anchor + every config knob + both feature flags) within ttl, then the persisted Redis snapshot for the ready anchor, then last-good, then an empty placeholder (and it calls trigger_warmer). It never computes inline.
The co-movement/schedule pass is cached per (week_start, knobs) and recomputed at most every cheaters_comovement_recompute_seconds (3600).
components.port_notes: Two switches: feature_cheater_detection_enabled (per-player checks) and feature_alt_clusters_enabled (name-stem + co-movement + schedule fusion). Both off returns a disabled payload. Per board: skip admin-excluded (cheaters_excluded_board_uuids CSV) and boards with < cheaters_min_board_size entries (recorded with reason admin_excluded/below_min_size). Direction is inferred from where rank-1's score sits. Lifetime cadence (default/none) runs velocity only. Score-outlier: log10(score+1) MAD-Z on the elite cohort max(50, n*cohort_pct), skipped if the top 5 are tied, checks the top max(10, cohort/2), z=0.6745*(x-med)/mad. Rank-gap: gaps over the top 3 vs the median tail gap, threshold 10x. Velocity: only for already-flagged players, peers are the top 50 with history in the same reset cycle floored at hot_window_start, p95 index max(0,int(0.95n)-1), needs >=5 samples. Sustained weekly uptime flags come from the history pass (needs >=48 slots). Clusters run _detect_clusters off-thread (board families via native det_board_families with a Python _name_stem callback for non-ASCII), then week-long co-movement/schedule via native det_history, then Python _merge_board_groups/_build_schedule_cluster/_fuse. Confidence: per-evidence sigmoid 0.5+0.5*(1-exp(-(ratio-1))) capped per type (velocity .99, sustained .95, rank_gap .85, score_outlier .60). Across boards it is noisy-OR, capped at the type ceiling if there is one type. Values pass through round(x,3). Output order: players sorted by (-confidence, -evidence count). analyzed/excluded boards sorted by (category.lower(), name.lower()). _round turns integral floats into int, otherwise round(v,2). Summary strings use Python formatting ('{:,}', '{:,.2f}', '{:.1f}', '{:.0f}%', '×' char), which must be reproduced exactly, including round-half-even on ties. WIRE: /v1 CheatersResponse drops cheater_detection_enabled/alt_clusters_enabled and coerces int scores to floats (1234 -> 1234.0); /site returns the raw dict (ints stay ints, extra keys kept). Cache-Control 'public, max-age={cheaters_cache_ttl_seconds}' on both. The tokenless public_scope('leaderboards:read') per-IP budget applies. recompute returns 202 {recomputing:true, redis_snapshots_cleared:n}. Note: ratio may be float('inf') when the median is 0 (JSON allow_nan=False would 500).
already_native: kiwi_native.det_board_families (kiwi-core detection::board_families/name_stem/merge_stems/edit_distance_le) with a Python name_stem fallback for non-ASCII

trove.stats class tables (class_index_for_board, class_pr/effort/paragon board uuid(s), class_name, class_icon, class_count) and trove.server_time merchant anchors/intervals.

core.internal_api.internal_get: the separate Python 3.13 gateway bot (no Postgres) calls /v1/activity/current, /v1/activity/series?period= and /site/market/items/{name}/summary over HTTP, so these contracts must stay stable through the port.
Website container (app.web) reads /site/feature-flags and the /site/leaderboards/* proxies; CSP/page allowlist and static asset versioning are outside this area but consume it.
hardest_parts: The cheater/alt-cluster detection pipeline (~2.4k lines of statistical heuristics). Only board families and the history producers are native. Score-outlier/rank-gap/velocity, cluster merge/fusion/confidence and the exact human-readable summary strings (Python format specs, round-half-even) are still Python. name_stem falls back to Python for non-ASCII names, so Unicode regex \s/\d and str.lower semantics must be reproduced.

Byte-exact JSON. Python float repr differs from serde/ryu ('1e+16' vs '1e16'). round() is banker's everywhere (t centroids, cadence buckets, effort_added, store interval days, mastery records). Pydantic /v1 models reorder, filter and coerce int->float (e.g. cheater scores 1234 -> 1234.0, activity series drops 'avg', profile drops renames/alt_clusters/duplicate/slots), while /site returns the raw dicts. Both shapes must be produced, often from the same cached Redis payload.

The ingest write path. One transaction over a ~700k-row COPY into a temp table, a COLLATE "C" player upsert, the partitioned entry insert, case-collision capture from the staging rows, and the player_board_agg fold, against a 1.5B-row partitioned table split across NVMe and a cold tablespace. Every read relies on carefully shaped SQL (recursive skip scans, player-id-first lookups, partition pruning) that must be kept verbatim to stay under the 120s timeout.

JSONB in player_rename/player_duplicate is very likely double-encoded (Python json.dumps passed through an asyncpg json.dumps codec, so it is stored as a jsonb string). The Rust reader must accept both string-wrapped and real jsonb (case-collision rows) and preserve key order. The SQL that compares evidence = '{}'::jsonb behaves differently for the two forms.

Warmer and serving semantics. The 'ready anchor' publish gate, persisted per-anchor snapshots, stale-but-good fallbacks, early wake on ingest, cold-tier drip and the resume-on-boot freshness probe all have to work. Python runs one independent warmer per uvicorn worker (8), so the Rust single-process design must pick a deliberate equivalent and stay Redis-compatible if both stacks run side by side during migration.

Python-exact parsing. The LeaderBot dump (Unicode digit ranks, the Python float() grammar, isspace stripping, Unicode \d in the market regex), StoreLog (str.splitlines line breaks, unquote) and market UUID v1 timestamps (float division above 2^53 can shift created_at by 1s) all need exact handling.

Hour-long replay/backfill jobs (agg rebuild with a table swap under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, last_rise backfill, rename/duplicate/activity/class backfills, backlog reingest). They need single-flight (Redis NX heartbeats, PG advisory lock), incremental flushing so they survive restarts, and live status payloads with fixed shapes.

summary: The mods area is the Mods Hub, a git-backed mod-sharing platform. It has per-project bare git repos served over authenticated smart-HTTP through dulwich, compiled .tmod/.zip releases kept in a SHA-256 content-addressed store, images with on-demand WebP thumbnails, profiles, stars, collaborators, forks/remixes, issues, hash lookup for desktop update checks, master moderation with DSA-style reports and takedowns, and an import of "stray" mods from an external catalog that users can then claim. Around it sit Modpacks (bundles of hub mods built on the fly into .tpack/.zip), the stateless Mod Workshop compiler, the custom-art intake plus a separate builder container that runs git, TroveUI's own Python scripts, the Flex SDK and FFDec on Java, and steamcmd, plus three small Steam/Trovesaurus mirrors (mod_stats, steam_workshop, btt_blocklist). In total it is about 13k lines of Python, roughly 1.3k more in site/admin route glue, and a 141 MB baked rig dataset. mods_hub/service.py alone is 3,944 lines of dict-shaped DTOs with many ordering and format quirks. kiwi_native already covers .tmod header/pack/contents, blueprint grid decoding and inflate. The two hard parts are git (no full Rust server implementation exists, so shell out to git) and the external-process builder, which cannot leave a Python/Java runtime because it runs another repo's Python scripts. The rest is a large but mechanical Mongo/axum port.

components.port_notes: DTOs are hand-built dicts, so key order is the wire order (use preserve_order serde_json or struct field order). Python `{**card, 'taken_down': x, 'mode': y}` overwrites IN PLACE and keeps the key at its original card position. serde flatten would emit duplicates, so merge by key. This applies to project_detail, master list cards, _stray_card, _remix_card, the get_release route ({**_release_dto, project_slug, project_handle, project_title}) and list_owned (+is_collaborator at the end). cards_with_avatars rewrites card['handle'] in place to the owner's CURRENT username and appends owner_avatar_url last. Datetimes are Python isoformat on tz-aware UTC: '+00:00' suffix, NO fraction when microsecond==0, otherwise exactly 6 digits. Documents read back from Mongo carry ms precision ('.123000+00:00'), but a freshly inserted doc returned in the same request (create_project/_insert_release) carries full µs, so chrono AutoSi is wrong. Commit created_at comes from an int timestamp, so it never has a fraction. Floats: popularity_score is round(x,4) and master list round(x,3); Python repr prints 1.0/0.0, and serde matches except for exponent forms. Visibility: effective_visibility() remix rules (pending for at least 7 days counts as public_website_only, denied counts as hidden). _browse_match is used by /v1/mods/hub/projects and tags. /v1/mods (public_list) is DIFFERENT: visibility=='public', taken_down False, is_remix != True, search merged at top level via query.update. The hub search is appended into $and. project_card hides 'public_website_only' as 'public' unless reveal. Unknown sort falls back to -updated_at; 'recent' sorts -last_release_at (Mongo nulls last on desc). tag_facets: fixed categories first in bit order, then custom sorted by (-count, tag.lower()). /me/stats rows are sorted by (-views, title.lower()). Status quirks: _require_owned answers 404 for non-editors, while service-level _require_owner answers 403. A draft viewed by a stranger is 404 with error code 'not_public', not 'not_found'. Profiles 404 unless the user has at least one public, non-taken-down mod. lookup: hashes are strip().lower() and de-duplicated in order; newest published release wins; it matches tmod_sha OR prior_tmod_shas; the returned 'unknown' and 'taken_down' lists keep input order; releases mode none/latest/all, where `releases` overrides `include_releases`. public_mod_dto builds absolute URLs from settings.api_url/app_url (rstrip '/'). Profile avatar url appends '?w=200' when small; the Discord fallback is cdn.discordapp.com/avatars/{id}/{hash}.{gif|png}?size=N, or embed/avatars/{(id>>22)%6}.png. Slugs: lowercase, [^a-z0-9]+ -> '-', 60 chars max, fallback 'mod', made unique per owner with -2, -3 and so on. Tags: lowercased, whitespace collapsed, 30 chars, max 12. URLs must match ^https?://\S+$ and be at most 300 chars. i18n maps only accept app.i18n.SUPPORTED minus 'en'; blanks are dropped. Writes mutate via save() except the deliberate atomic $inc/$set paths (stars, downloads, popularity, issue counters); keep those atomic. The /site proxies set Cache-Control: projects public max-age=30, tags 60, modders 300, detail/profile/me no-cache. Global middleware OVERWRITES Cache-Control with 'private, no-store' and adds Vary: Cookie, Authorization whenever the request carries an Authorization header or the kiwi_site_access cookie. Feature flag feature_mods_hub_enabled 404s every /v1/mods/hub, /v1/mods, /git route. Axum route-precedence trap: FastAPI falls through /v1/mods/hub/<x> to GET /v1/mods/{handle}/{slug} when <x> is not a hub route (handle 'hub'). Check that matchit backtracks the same way.
