components.port_notes: Release artifact identity is the sha256 of the stored bytes (CAS key). Hash uniqueness gates: _ensure_hash_unowned blocks if another owner (owner_id $nin [None, me]) has the hash in tmod_sha OR prior_tmod_shas. Uploaded-on-behalf mods use the global check (any other project_id). A config repack moves the old sha into prior_tmod_shas. Compile from commit: only trove_layout-compilable paths are read from git. tmod properties in INSERTION order: title, author (comma list normalized, 200 chars), modVersion=tag, notes (if changelog), tags (comma-joined), flags (if any category), then previewPath/configPath when injected, then modLoader appended last (or kept in place on repack). Header byte order matters for the sha, so use kiwi_core::tmod::pack, which is already byte-compatible. Preview is packed at ui/<safe(slug)>.<png|jpg|gif> lowercased; WebP is refused. Config is packed at ui/<safe(title)>.cfg with case KEPT, max 256 KiB, no NUL bytes, only if the build ships a .swf. Branch for compile = ref if it names a branch, else the default branch. Upload detection: zip if the bytes start with 'PK' or the filename ends with .zip. Download filename = '<safe(title prop)>.tmod' (zip keeps the stored name). _safe_filename strips [<>:"/\\|?*\x00-\x1f], strips spaces and dots, max 120 chars, fallback 'mod'. Starlette encodes header values as latin-1, so a Content-Disposition with CJK in the title 500s today (decide whether to keep that or move to RFC 5987). Media types: zip application/zip, else application/octet-stream; .cfg text/plain; charset=utf-8. /v1 download sets no Cache-Control; the /site variant sets no-cache. VFX list max-age=60, manifest 120, asset 3600; audio list 60, bank 300, sound 86400 + ETag '"<sha>[-raw]"' with exact If-None-Match compare (304 with ETag only). bp_cache.respond: Cache-Control public, max-age=300; Vary: Accept-Encoding; X-Kiwi-Cache; Server-Timing bpcache;desc=...;dur=...; ETag of the gz blob sha; serves stored gzip verbatim when Accept-Encoding includes gzip, else decompresses; fmt=bin is the KVX1 binpack. Cache keys: PACK_VERSION 'v3:tmod:<sha>:<lowercased path>', assembly key includes the rig_index signature '<branch>:<parser_version>:<unix updated_at>'. inspect sorts files by path.lower(); cfgs sort by (not declared, path.lower()); files list excludes previewPath (case-insensitive). release_with_project: drafts are visible only to the PRIMARY owner (not collaborators). PATCH/DELETE release routes 404 unless project.owner_id == user. attach config has no router owner check and the service answers 403 for non-editors. Event payload (bus.publish) is json.dumps(default=str) with Python default separators and ensure_ascii; it carries project (public_mod_dto minus description/readme), release (public_release_dto + id/status/source_commit_sha/properties/mod_version/mod_author/image_url/created_at), previous, change{kind,is_first_release,from_tag,to_tag,size_delta,days_since_previous=round(days,2),release_count,artifact_unchanged}, image_url, download_url, page_url. Announce only when visibility=='public' AND not taken down AND not remix AND the branch is not hidden AND announced_at is null. Silent releases are stamped announced without publishing. _announce_newly_visible emits only the newest pending build and stamps the rest.

python_deps: dulwich (Repo, commit_tree, iter_tree_contents, get_walker, UploadPackHandler, ReceivePackHandler, pkt_line) -> git CLI subprocess for protocol (`git upload-pack --stateless-rpc`, `git receive-pack --stateless-rpc`, or `git http-backend`) + gix or git2 for local object/ref ops
components.port_notes: Protocol: info/refs needs ?service=git-upload-pack|git-receive-pack. Anything else is 403 forbidden; a missing param is FastAPI's 422. The body is pkt_line('# service=<svc>\n') + '0000' + stateless advertisement. Content-Types are application/x-<svc>-advertisement and application/x-<svc>-result. Headers are Cache-Control 'no-cache, max-age=0, must-revalidate' and Pragma no-cache, but the middleware rewrites this to 'private, no-store' + Vary when Authorization is present. Auth is HTTP Basic; only the password (git token, prefix 'kgit_') matters, and it is looked up by sha256 hex with revoked False; this bumps last_used_at; the user must be active. Unknown repo: 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Kiwi Mods Hub git" when anonymous, otherwise 404. Push requires the PRIMARY owner (403 otherwise; collaborators cannot push). Clone requires source_visible (files mode + public source, or editor). The path segment is '{slug}.git'. axum/matchit may not capture a param with a literal suffix in one segment, so capture the segment and strip '.git' (404 if absent). Push guard: dulwich applies the pack, then rewinds any ref whose new tip tree contains a *.tmod (case-insensitive) and reports 'ng <ref> a built .tmod belongs in a release, not in the files (<path>)'. A Rust port can use a pre-receive/update hook (cleaner; message format differs slightly) or reproduce the rewind. Latent issue (plausible, unverified): request bodies are not gunzipped, and git clients send Content-Encoding: gzip on larger upload-pack POSTs, so a Rust port should decode it. Web commit: adds normalized by _norm_path (lowercase, backslash->/, no ./.., max 255 bytes), mode 100644, .tmod refused, max 500 files, max 20 MB per file (413 with code bad_request). NothingToCommit becomes 400. Commit author is '<display_name or username> <sanitized@users.noreply.kiwi>', tz 0, encoding UTF-8, message stripped or '(no message)'. Fork copies only the default-branch HEAD tree into ONE new commit (no history) with message 'Fork of <slug>'. Commit DTO: {id, short (7), branch, parents, author_username, message (stripped), file_count (recursive blob count per commit, expensive), created_at isoformat from int ts}. list_commits uses the dulwich walker (date order) with max_entries=offset+limit, slices, and counts the total by walking the full history. Tree entries {path, blob_sha, size} sorted by path. compare returns sorted added/removed/modified by blob sha. Empty repo/unknown ref: tree returns {commit:null, entries:[]}; branches returns a synthetic [{name: default_branch, head_commit_id: null}]. Branch names: [A-Za-z0-9._/-]{1,80}, no leading '/', no '..'; deleting the default branch is refused. Source archive filename is safe('<slug>-<ref or default>-<sha7>').zip. Placement report shape {commit,total,compilable_count,skipped[{path,reason}],misplaced[{path,expected}],fix_available,game_index_available}; skipped excludes misplaced. fix-placement makes one commit 'Fix file placement (N file[s])'. Git token DTO {id,name,prefix(raw[:12]),created_at,last_used_at}; create returns {...dto, token}.

components.port_notes: Every /admin route is behind get_current_superuser; assign/claims approve/reject also take the admin id. Takedown sets the reason (default 'Removed by a moderator.'), records every release sha (tmod_sha + prior) into mod_taken_down_artifacts with upsert $setOnInsert created_at, resolves open reports, and emails the owner's notify_email only if set. A new mod from a bulk import is approved and public; from a resync it is pending and draft. The release filename is '<title prop>.tmod' (not sanitized), else '<slugify(title)>.<fmt>'. Author = .tmod header author, else the catalog username. handover_stray re-slugs on a clash, sets visibility public, and stamps releases announced so they never fire events. approve_claim auto-rejects other pending claims (without resolved_by). The admin_assign_stray result is {assigned[{id,slug}], errors[{id,error}], owner_handle, owner_username}. components.name: mods_hub content-addressed store, images, thumbnails
data: disk <mods_store_dir>/objects/<sha[:2]>/<sha> (default data/mods; prod /data/mods bind ./.mods); temp '*.part' files in the shard dir, fsync + os.replace
Mongo mod_images (sha unique; variants map str(width)->CAS sha)
python_deps: Pillow Image.open/LANCZOS/WEBP q=82 method=4 -> image + fast_image_resize (premultiplied Lanczos3) + webp (libwebp) for lossy encode
numpy premultiply/unpremultiply -> plain loops or fast_image_resize alpha mul/div
components.port_notes: The CAS is shared with bp_cache, modpack custom uploads and custom_art pictures. put is idempotent (returns created=false if the file exists). Upload sniffing uses magic bytes only (PNG, GIF87a/89a, RIFF..WEBP, JPEG SOF scan); width/height are best effort (null if unparsed); minimum 24 bytes; max mods_image_max_bytes 5 MB (413 with code bad_request); 'Unsupported image - use PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF.' is 400. A duplicate upload returns the existing ModImageAsset (owner unchanged). Thumbnails: w must be in (200,400,708,1416), else 400 'w must be one of 200, 400, 708, 1416'. A variant is rendered on first request, stored in the CAS, and recorded with a targeted $set variants.<w> (race-safe). It returns None (serve original) for animated images, images already narrow and already WebP, Pillow failures, or re-encodes that are not below 75% of the original size. Resize keeps the height as round(h*w/W) with minimum 1 and uses premultiplied alpha when the image has alpha (including P mode with transparency). Output will not be byte-identical to Pillow; that is fine because existing variants keep serving from the recorded map. Headers: Cache-Control 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'; media type = stored content_type, or image/webp for a variant. /site/mods/image errors use HTTPException (fallback envelope).

hardest_parts: Git smart-HTTP: dulwich implements upload-pack/receive-pack in-process, and gitoxide has no complete server-side receive-pack, so the Rust side should shell out to `git upload-pack/receive-pack --stateless-rpc` (or git http-backend). The .tmod push guard (dulwich applies the pack then rewinds the ref and reports a custom 'ng' line) has to be reproduced, as do Basic-token auth with the 401/404 existence-hiding rules and the '{slug}.git' segment routing. Request gzip bodies need handling too, since the Python version appears to mishandle them today.

Local git operations for the web studio (flat-path tree building with preserved modes, walker order and pagination, recursive file_count per commit, fork-as-single-commit, branch create/delete, blob reads) via gix/git2, matching dulwich's outputs and DTOs exactly.

The size and subtlety of mods_hub/service.py (3.9k lines): Python dict-merge key-order semantics, isoformat datetimes whose fraction width depends on whether the doc was just inserted or read back from Mongo, remix effective-visibility, the exactly-once release-announcement state machine, 403-vs-404-vs-not_public status choices that differ route by route, and two different catalog queries (hub _browse_match vs /v1/mods public_list).

The artifact pipeline must stay hash-stable: .tmod property insertion order (modLoader appended or kept in place), config/preview injection paths and case rules, repack with prior_tmod_shas, cross-owner/global hash-uniqueness checks, and lookup matching both current and prior hashes. kiwi_core::tmod::pack must remain byte-identical to the Python builder.

Rig assembly: numpy matrix math (bake, enclosed-emissive unbury) must be ported in f64. The 141 MB baked rigs dataset ships alongside, the first-row-wins semantics depend on the Postgres ORDER BY, and float JSON formatting differs between Python repr and ryu inside bp_cache payloads (needs a cache-generation bump or a Python-compatible float writer).

Pillow parity for thumbnails (LANCZOS on premultiplied alpha, lossy WebP q82 method 4, the 75%-smaller rule, animated/narrow fallbacks) needs libwebp via the webp crate. Output bytes will differ, so rely on the recorded variants map.

The custom-art builder container cannot become pure Rust: it runs TroveUI's Python scripts (which need the Flex SDK and FFDec on Java), the git CLI and 32-bit steamcmd. At most the poll/orchestration loop moves to Rust; the runtime stays polyglot. The SWF code view similarly stays a Java FFDec subprocess.

Background work scattered across per-worker in-process state (lazy popularity refresh, game-file-map cache, rig-map cache, VFX dep-set cache, stray import task, Steam refresher with no cross-worker lock) needs explicit single-leader or idempotent designs in Rust.

Known defects to fix rather than replicate: issues.delete_comment calls to_oid(event_id, "event id") but to_oid takes one argument, so the endpoint 500s every time. strayimport._FILE_DELAY is defined but never applied. Content-Disposition with non-latin-1 titles 500s under Starlette's latin-1 header encoding.

summary: The trove_v1 area is the public /v1 data surface of the API container. app/trove/router.py is a single 3,811-line module that declares 15 APIRouters: rotations, feeds, stats, gems, misc, mods, updates, codexes, btt, leaderboards, market, store, activity, class-activity and ocr. Two more routers live next to it: dressing (/v1/dressing) and moderation (/v1/moderation). The services that belong to this area are deterministic rotation and calendar math, bot-captured rotations (chaos chest, challenge, Luxion), upstream relays (trovegame.com RSS, the Trovesaurus calendar and chaos chest, Twitch Helix, the YouTube Data API, a Bilibili HTML scrape, GitHub releases and commits, an external delve source), the Trove server-status prober (HTTPS login probe plus a raw TCP glsserver handshake), the stateless gem simulator, evaluator and build optimiser, static game-reference tables (classes, stat tables, the sigil PNG), misc time and feedback tools, the dressing-room catalogue and model, and the tomes valuation. In total it is about 14k Python lines: roughly 8k of real logic and 6k of route-layer and schema code. About 40% of the routes in router.py (leaderboards, market, store, updates, codexes, ocr, mods) are thin handlers over services that other areas own. Everything except the dressing room and the route layers over other areas is self-contained and an S/M-sized port. The real cost is byte-for-byte JSON parity with pydantic-core: float formatting, three different datetime formats, response-model field projection and computed-field ordering. Smaller costs are Python round() and datetime/zoneinfo semantics, and OpenAPI parity (184 paths, 279 schemas, including FastAPI's Gem-Input/Gem-Output split).

ENDPOINT SHAPES
- All of it is pure functions over now(): biome_rotation (3h d15 epoch 2024-06-18T11:00Z, three parallel lists indexed by offset % len), wild_mana, stampy (base 2023-09-30T11:00Z, 48h), corruxion/fluxion (anchors in trove-time frame = UTC-11h), gardening, yearly_calendar (+/-365d), challenge_window.
- Copy the anchor constants and lists verbatim. The indexes depend on list lengths: _BIOME1=12, _BIOME2=11, _BIOME3=14 entries (duplicates included).

WIRE TRAPS
- ServerTime.now_iso is Python datetime.isoformat() of the aware UTC now: '2026-10-22T12:34:56.123456+00:00'. It uses '+00:00', not Z, and the fractional part is omitted entirely when microsecond == 0.
- trove_day is strftime('%A') in English.
- Luxion: starts_at/ends_at are null with an empty schedule until the first capture. starts_at is the first_seen instant, not the stored day anchor.
- Luxion: schedule entries carry state 'Day N' and sit on a 27h grid from 2025-10-10T11:00Z, clipped to the run. LUXION_RUN_DAYS=7.
- Luxion: first_seen_at/last_seen_at are Mongo datetimes, serialized pydantic-style.
- luxion/history.started_at is run_bounds(...)[0], i.e. the first-sighting unix time.
- Chaos: build_response drops a cached relay item whose end <= now.
- Chaos: the bot capture for the current Tue-11:00-anchored week (computed off FIRST_FLUXION+11h) wins over the relay.
- Chaos: item.image_url is f'{api_url}/v1/codexes/render?blueprint={quote(bp, safe="")}&dim=256'.
- Chaos: fetched_at is null when item is null.
- The chaos blueprint memo is per-process and never invalidated (misses are cached too).
- classify_challenge literals are an exact-match public contract: 'Collection Challenge'->collection, 'RAMPAGE ALERT!'->rampage, 'Racing Challenge'->racing, 'Target Challenge'->target, anything else->dungeon.
- challenge/insert rejects '' or 'none' (case-insensitive) with 400 bad_request.
- history limits: challenge le=500; chaos and luxion le=200.
- calendar events are sorted by (starts_at, type string). CalendarEvent always carries all 7 keys: color/state/biomes are null when absent.
- gardening.upcoming is stable-sorted by starts_at and capped at 10.
- stampy.current can be null.
- delves: 404 not_found only when ?week= is given and missing. A missing current week returns an empty rotation with fetched_at null.
- delves: depths is list[dict] passed through raw from Mongo. Preserve key order and int/float typing (bson -> serde_json with preserve_order).
- current_week_id = (now in UTC-11 - 2025-11-03T00:00-11:00).days // 7 + 1.

INSERT ROUTES
- Master token required.
- Bodies: {name}, or an optional {active: true} (the Luxion body may be absent).
- Response: CaptureInsertResponse {anchor, name, refreshed}. A Luxion no-op close returns anchor 0 and name 'luxion:away'.
- Each insert then calls the events bus best-effort (errors swallowed).

FEATURE GATE
- Delves routes carry an extra per-route gate (require_delves_enabled -> 404).

Redis events:sig:trove_news + PUBLISH kiwi:events (the news refresher calls bus.publish_type('trove_news'))
Env TWITCH_CLIENT_ID/TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET/YT_API_KEY, twitch_game_id=412756

Feed refresh: every trove_feeds_refresh_seconds (300s). Twitch: client-credentials token (cached in-process, re-minted on 401) then Helix /streams?game_id&first=100. YouTube: search.list (maxResults 50, publishedAfter) then videos.list enrich, then curation filters (Shorts <=60s or #shorts dropped). Bilibili: search page scrape. Per-feed errors are swallowed and the last good payload is kept.

components.port_notes:
NEWS
- /feeds/news over-fetches limit*3 rows sorted -published_at, dedups by lower(trim(title)) (url fallback), and merges later duplicates' categories into the kept doc in order.
- summary = _truncate(_strip_html(unescape(description)), 220): cut at the last space, then '...' appended.
- author defaults to 'Team Trove'; category defaults to 'News' (otherwise the first <category>).
- parsedate_to_datetime returns a NAIVE datetime for a '-0000' zone, and Python then .astimezone() treats it as host-local time (edge quirk).

FEED PAYLOADS
- Items are stored pre-normalized and served through the TwitchStream/Video models.
- TwitchStream key order: channel, login, url, title, viewers, game, started_at, thumbnail.
- Video key order: title, url, channel, video_id, published_at, thumbnail_url.
- published_at/started_at are passthrough STRINGS from upstream.
- Bilibili builds them as isoformat().replace('+00:00','Z') of utcnow-derived datetimes, so relative dates carry 6-digit microseconds ('...56.123456Z') and absolute dates do not.
- fetched_at is a Mongo datetime, serialized pydantic-style.
- Twitch thumbnails replace {width}/{height} with 440/248.

BILIBILI IMAGE PROXY
- Only https://*.hdslb.com URLs; anything else -> 400 bad_request. Redirects are not followed.
- Sends Referer https://www.bilibili.com/ and a Chrome UA.
- A non-image/* upstream content-type is coerced to image/jpeg.
- Response header: Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400.
- An httpx error -> 502 with code internal_error and message 'upstream thumbnail fetch failed: {exc}'.
- Isolated rate-limit bucket (public_scope feeds:read, rate_multiplier=bilibili_image_rate_limit_multiplier=10).

EVENTS
- status/seconds_until are computed per request: upcoming -> starts-now, ongoing -> ends-now, else 0.
- Sorts: ongoing ends_at asc; upcoming starts_at asc; history ends_at desc.
- limit 1..500, default 100.
- categories = Mongo $group on category then $sort _id asc; falsy _id values are dropped.

NEWS HISTORY
- Token-only (misc:read), paginated via count + skip/limit, sorted -published_at.

SCOPES
- All feeds:read routes are public (tokenless at the anon per-IP budget).

components.port_notes:
SCOPES AND STATUS CODES
- power-rank/magic-find/light/classes need a stats:read token.
- coefficient and sigil are public_scope('stats:read').
- Unknown tech_name -> 404 not_found "No class with tech_name '{x}'".

CLASS PROJECTION
- _clean_class/_clean_ability emit levels, energy, cooldown, healing, effects, vfx and extra stage keys, but the TroveClass/Ability/AbilityStage response models DROP all of them.
- Served shape, exactly: tech_name, name, shorts, damage_type, weapons, attributes, stats, bonuses, subclass{name, description, level{str->[ClassStat]}, power{str->str}}, abilities[{name, description, icon, type, prefab, active, stages[{name, base, multiplier, prefab}]}]. Reproduce this projection.
- Class order = classes.json order.
- Abilities fall back to class_abilities.json keyed by display name when the class entry has none.

FLOAT FIELDS
- StatSource.value/step, ClassStat.value and AbilityStage.base/multiplier are float-typed, so integral JSON numbers serialize as 10.0 / 0.0.
- 'permanent' comes from the source key 'perm'; type defaults to 'switch'.

COEFFICIENT
- Formula: int(round(max(phys, magic) * (1 + crit/100), 6)), i.e. Python round-half-even to 6 places, then truncate. Use kiwi_core::gems::py_round.
- Response: {coefficient, damage_used, formula} where formula is the literal COEFFICIENT_FORMULA string.
- Missing inputs -> 400 bad_request. Negative values -> 422 (ge=0).

SIGIL
- tier = max index whose 'from' <= value.
- The mastery layer is drawn under the power_rank layer; both are base64 PNGs in insignia.json.
- Responds image/png with Cache-Control public, max-age=86400.
- 503 service_unavailable 'Sigil art is not available yet' when insignia.json is missing.
- Query bounds: power_rank 0..10,000,000; mastery 0..100,000.

LEADERBOARDS HELPERS

components.port_notes:
SCOPE AND ERRORS
- All routes need a gems:read token.
- Invalid enum ints in query params -> 400 bad_request (ValueError mapping). In bodies they are pydantic 422s.
- Evaluator/BuildError/ValueError/KeyError/ZeroDivisionError -> 400 bad_request with message prefixes 'Invalid gem parameters: ', 'Could not evaluate gem: ', 'Invalid level-cost parameters: ', 'Invalid stat-range parameters: '. The messages embed Python exception text (e.g. KeyError repr), which a port can only approximate.

GEM WIRE OBJECT (field order matters)
- Gem stored fields: id, tier, type, element, restriction, ability, level, stats, augmentation, attempts, karma, spent.
- Gem computed fields follow them: ability_name, gem_name, is_max_level, quality, power_rank, stat_values.
- StatContainer: base, augments[{type, count}], then computed increase, value, real_value.
- Stat: type, containers, locked, then computed augmentation_progress.
- IntEnums serialize as ints. stat_values is [{display_name: float}].
- On input, computed fields are ignored. A container posted WITHOUT 'base' gets a fresh random base (default_factory=random).
- id defaults to int(now*100).

ROUNDING
- quality = round(avg*100, 1)/100.
- power_rank = round() to int, half-even.
- karma_gain = floor(round(x*100, 6)).
- level_plan: expected_attempts round(..., 2); expected_total counts use round() half-even.
- The evaluator uses round(..., 4/2/9) heavily.
- Reuse kiwi_core::gems::py_round, which already implements exact Python rounding.

BUILDS
- calculate_builds already calls kiwi_native.gem_rank (kiwi-core/src/gems.rs, top 200).
- Still Python: _format and the pre-rank stat assembly (food/ally/Lilypad multipliers, star-chart parser, class bonuses).
- generate_combinations order is product(first10, second19, third, fourth); the Light build yields 190 results.
- LATENT BUG: BuildResult.light is typed int, but the value is rd(cthird*sixth/100, 2), a float such as 12544.5. With current gamedata, POST /v1/gems/builds/calculate with the default Bard/Boomeranger config raises a pydantic ValidationError inside the handler and returns 500. The /site/gems/builds/calculate proxy bypasses the model and works. Decide in the port: type light as f64 (fix) or keep int.
- BuildResult.crit_bonus, class_bonus and other float fields render as x.0.

HEALTH OPTIMIZER
- Enumerates combinations_with_replacement(range(3), 3) x (range(3), 6).
- Sort key (-health, crit).
- Result field order: rank, layout, empowered, lesser, critical_hit, maximum_health, maximum_health_per, health (HealthOptimizerResult inherits HealthTotals first).

LOOKUPS
- abilities_by_element keys are display names ('Water', ...).
- boosters are projected to id, name, chance_multiplier, double_multiplier.
- empowered_gems comes from gem_abilities.json through the EmpoweredGem model (another field projection).
already_native: kiwi_core::gems::py_round available for every rounding call

components.port_notes:
SCOPES
- public_scope misc:read for every route except feedback.
- feedback has no scope dependency at all and is marked openapi_extra x-tokenless.

TIME CONVERTER
- Zone list order is fixed: trove (UTC-11 fixed), UTC, then 9 IANA zones.
- ZoneTime.datetime = Python isoformat() of fromtimestamp(int): no fractional part, offsets like '-11:00' / '+00:00' / '-03:00'.
- date = strftime('%b %d, %Y') ('Jun 05, 2026', English); time = '%H:%M:%S'.
- iso_utc ends in '+00:00'.
- discord codes are '<t:{unix}:{t|T|d|D|f|F|R}>' with fixed labels.
- Input parsing accepts anything Python 3.11+ datetime.fromisoformat accepts: date-only, space separator, 'Z', basic format, offsets.
- An aware input ignores timezone.
- A naive input is replace(tzinfo=ZoneInfo(...)) with fold=0: ambiguous DST times take the FIRST offset, and spring-forward gaps take the PRE-transition offset. chrono-tz returns None/Ambiguous in those cases, so emulate Python's behaviour.
- An unknown timezone -> 400 "Unknown timezone '{id}'." (validated only when unix is absent).

FEEDBACK REQUEST
- Multipart form fields: message, contact (<=200), category, app_version (<=64), attachments[] (up to 4 files).
- message outside 5..2000 -> 422 from FastAPI validation.
- category outside {bug, feature, general} -> 400 bad_request, not 422.
- After stripping, a message under 5 chars -> 400 from MiscError.
- UA is truncated to 300, then parsed to os/client labels by ordered regex rules (Android before Linux; BetterTroveTools/Edge/Opera/Brave before Chrome).

FEEDBACK RATE LIMITS
- Per-IP bucket first; its X-RateLimit-* headers are copied onto the success response.
- Then the global bucket.
- 429 carries Retry-After.

FEEDBACK ATTACHMENTS
- MIME must be png/jpeg/webp/gif.
- Zero-byte parts are silently skipped.
- Over 5 MB -> 400.
- Filenames are sanitised with re.sub(r'[^\w.\-]', '_', basename)[:80] or 'image'. Python \w is Unicode-aware.

FEEDBACK RESPONSE
- FeedbackAck {ok: true, received_at}.
- received_at is the in-memory utcnow, NOT round-tripped through Mongo, so it carries full 6-digit microseconds plus Z.

DISCORD PAYLOAD
- Embed colour by category: bug 0xf85149, feature 0xd29922, general 0x58a6ff.
- title 'New {category} feedback'; description truncated at 1500 + ' …'.
- Inline fields OS / Client / App version (256 chars), plus a non-inline Contact (1024 chars).
- footer 'id {doc_id}'; timestamp is isoformat with '+00:00'.
- Attachments are renamed '{i}_{name}' and sent as files[i] alongside payload_json.
- Every image embed shares url https://api.aallyn.net/feedback/{id} so Discord groups them into one card.

components.name: Trove server status prober
data: Mongo trove_status_events (TroveStatusEvent; index env asc + started_at desc; open segment has ended_at null)
Redis key kiwi:status:current (JSON snapshot, EX 600; read by the bot via get_status_shared)
Redis events:sig:server_status + PUBLISH kiwi:events (bus.publish_type('server_status') after every probe)
In-process _state snapshot (served by the GET endpoint)

Mongo runtime_config keys trove_status_{eu,us,pts}_host/_port/_hello_hex, trove_status_probe_attempts, trove_status_probe_retry_delay_seconds, trove_status_game_deep_probe, trove_status_game_hold_seconds, trove_status_game_random_opener, trove_status_local_check_enabled/_hosts/_timeout_seconds
background: Status prober loop: starts 3s after boot, probes, then sleeps trove_status_probe_interval_seconds (60s).

Each probe POSTs https://auth.trionworlds.com/auth/v1_2 with empty creds, the Glyph UA and form fields username/password/channel=131/includeStoreToken/publicMachine=0/macAddr=000000000000. It counts as up when the reply is Trion-shaped (any x-trionworlds* header or 'Signature:' in the body); a 404 or 5xx is down; any other code is up.

Per env eu/us/pts it then TCP-connects host:6560. When deep probing applies it sends a 0x20 0 0 0 0 header plus 32 random bytes and holds up to hold_seconds: a timeout means online, a near-empty close (<=256 bytes) means down, and a reset is inconclusive and falls back to online.
Each probe retries up to N times back-to-back.
Blackout guard: when auth and all envs are down and none of 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9/8.8.8.8:443 answers, the round is discarded.
Today it runs in EVERY uvicorn worker (8), each with its own _state and each writing segments, so segment writes are duplicated and racy.
components.port_notes:
SNAPSHOT SHAPE
- Top level: {overall, auth, environments, checked_at}.
- auth = {online, http_status, latency_ms (round 1), error}.
- environments keeps insertion order eu, us, pts. Each is {status, online, game}.
- game = {online, host, port, latency_ms, error, probe ('tcp'|'tcp_fallback'|'glsserver'), opener ('random'|'replay')}. Key presence varies by path: a refused connection has no probe/opener; tcp has no opener.
- auth and environments are untyped dicts, so exact keys and insertion order pass straight through.
- Before the first probe: overall 'unknown', auth null, each env {status: 'unknown', online: false, game: null}, checked_at null.
- overall rolls up eu+us only.

HEADERS
- Cache-Control public, max-age=30 (current) and max-age=60 (history).
- The security middleware overwrites these to private,no-store for credentialed callers.

HISTORY
- The env query must match ^(live|pts)$, but get_history maps anything not in (eu, us, pts) to 'eu'. So ?env=live returns env 'eu' (compat quirk).
- days 1..90.
- Segments are clamped to the window. The open segment keeps ended_at null while its duration counts to now.
- uptime = round(up/covered, 5), or null.
- outages are the non-online segments, without the online key.
- Segments are read with sort +started_at over the whole env; the query has no window filter.

FEATURE GATE
- Both routes carry require_server_status_enabled (-> 404).

RUST
- Run one prober task per process (or leader-elected) and keep the Redis mirror for the bot.

Mongo btt_changelogs (BttChangelog singleton per repo)
Mongo steam_workshop_items + btt_mod_blocklist (via app.steam_workshop.service.catalog / app.btt_blocklist.service.served; other area)

background: BTT refresh: every btt_releases_refresh_seconds (1800s). GET /repos/{repo}/releases?per_page=100 and upsert by release_id (drafts skipped). Then tags?per_page=100 + commits?per_page=100, build the changelog groups and store the singleton. Each half is error-isolated. A rate-limit dict body sets rate_limited and keeps the old groups.
components.port_notes:
SCOPE
- btt:read, public.

PLATFORM MATCHING
- windows: .msi > .exe. linux: .appimage > .deb > .rpm > .tar.gz. android: .apk. Case-insensitive endswith.
- Matched assets sort by (priority, name).
- latest_per_platform walks releases newest-first, per platform independently.
- The platforms dict order is windows, linux, android, with null when a platform has no asset.

VALIDATION
- channel must be 'release' or 'beta', else 400.
- Unknown platform -> 404.
- /latest/{platform} with no matching asset -> 404 'no {channel} release carries a {platform} asset yet'.

VERSION COMPARE
- Regex ^v?(\d{1,9}(?:\.\d{1,9}){0,9})(.*)$; inputs longer than 64 chars are rejected.
- Numeric tuples are zero-padded to equal length.
- A release (no suffix) beats a prerelease; two suffixes compare as Python strings.
- update_available = cmp < 0; comparable = cmp is not None.

CHANGELOG
- Groups start with 'Unreleased'; a new group starts at each tagged sha; empty groups are dropped.
- Commit = {sha, short_sha (7 chars), message (first line), type (conventional prefix lowercased, or null), url}.
- limit_groups / commits_per_group: 0 means all.
- No doc yet -> {repo, groups: [], rate_limited: false, fetched_at: now}.

FIELD ORDERS
- BttReleaseMeta: release_id, tag_name, name, body, html_url, prerelease, channel (derived), published_at, fetched_at.
- BttReleaseInfo appends assets.
- BttAsset: name, url, size, content_type, download_count.

WORKSHOP
- BttWorkshopCatalog.fetched_at is a STRING built with Python isoformat ('...+00:00' with microseconds), unlike the pydantic datetime fields.

MOD BLOCKLIST
- hashes = dict.fromkeys(blocklist hashes in created_at order + sorted takedown md5s): an order-preserving dedup.
- workshop_items / workshop_authors default to [].

components.port_notes:
SCOPE AND GATE
- public_scope('codexes:read').
- Router-level gate require_dressing_room_enabled.
- The OpenAPI tag is 'dressing room' (with a space).
- An empty catalogue (no classes, or Postgres disabled) -> HTTP 503 with code 'not_found'. Keep or fix this status/code mismatch deliberately.

INPUT
- Selection values are trimmed and lowercased; longer than 220 -> 400.

/options
- slot must match ^(costume|hat|face|weapon|head|hair|eyes)$.
- costume without a valid class -> 400.
- weapon is filtered to the class's socket slots; head/eyes are filtered to the race's pieces.
- q is a substring match on the lowercased name or the key.
- Paging is offset/limit (1..500); total is the pre-page count.

/outfit
- Returns DressOutfit serialized BY ALIAS, so the first key is 'class'.
- Key order: class, costume, hat, face, weapon, head, hair, eyes, race, hair_color, eye_color, dropped, issues.
- issues = [{slot, value, reason}], reason in unknown|no_socket|missing_asset|covered.
- /image and /model set X-Dressing-Dropped ('hat=unknown,face=covered'), exposed via CORS expose_headers.

/image
- size 32..512 (default 256); az -360..360 (default 30); el -89..89 (default 8).
- Headers: Cache-Control 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'; ETag '"{sha256(png)[:32]}"'.

/model

- Build a golden-corpus test against real Python output.

hardest_parts:
Byte-exact JSON parity with pydantic-core dump_json:
- Float formatting differs from both ryu and Python repr: 1e+16, 0.00001, integral floats as x.0, NaN/Inf as null.
- Three coexisting datetime formats: pydantic 'Z' with 6-digit microseconds omitted when zero; Python isoformat '+00:00' in ServerTime.now_iso, ZoneTime.datetime, iso_utc, BttWorkshopCatalog.fetched_at and the moderation/admin lists; upstream passthrough strings in the feeds.
- Response-model projection silently drops keys, e.g. TroveClass loses levels/energy/cooldown/healing/effects/vfx.
- Computed fields are appended after stored fields (Gem, Stat, StatContainer), and DressOutfit serializes by alias ('class').

Python numeric semantics in gems: round() half-even on exact binary values (quality, power_rank, evaluator, level plan, coefficient, karma_gain), floor division, and itertools enumeration order that decides ranking ties. kiwi-core's py_round covers rounding, but the evaluator, level plan, health optimizer and the build pre-processing (food/ally/Lilypad/star-chart parser including the non-validating legacy base64 decode) are still Python.

Latent bug to resolve in the port: POST /v1/gems/builds/calculate returns 500 for the default Bard/Boomeranger config because BuildResult.light is typed int while the value is fractional (12544.5). The /site proxy works because it bypasses the model.

/v1/misc/time/convert must replicate Python 3.11+ datetime.fromisoformat leniency and zoneinfo fold=0 handling of DST gaps and overlaps (chrono-tz returns None/Ambiguous there), plus tzdata version drift.

Dressing room (XL): coupled to the codex binfab parsers, the Postgres rig_binding/codex_meta tables, the update_state + CAS archive, mods_hub assembly, bp_cache (Mongo blueprint_cache + CAS), and the numba voxel rasterizer for /image. Cache identities (Outfit.ident, Redis render:dress:* keys, bp_cache keys) must be reproduced, or invalidated with a version bump.

Status prober fidelity:
- Raw glsserver TCP deep probe with a random 0x20-framed opener and hold/close heuristics.
- The Trion-shaped auth check and the blackout guard against uplink loss.
- Segment transitions plus the Redis mirror for the bot.
- Today it runs in all 8 workers with per-worker in-process snapshots and racy duplicate segment writes; Rust should consolidate to one prober.

Upstream relays with scraping and quota concerns: YouTube Data API curation (word-boundary Unicode regexes, Shorts filtering, per-channel caps), Bilibili HTML scrape with Chinese relative-date parsing, the lenient RSS pubDate parsing, the Twitch app-token refresh on 401, GitHub rate-limit handling. All refreshers currently run 8x per cycle (one per worker).

OpenAPI parity for the public reference: 184 paths and 279 component schemas, FastAPI/pydantic naming quirks (Gem-Input/Gem-Output), tokenless and master markers, x-tokenless, tag order, servers, and runtime pruning of feature-gated operations. A utoipa regeneration will not match byte-for-byte; a snapshot is the practical route.

Non-Rust runtimes reachable from this area: RapidOCR/onnxruntime behind /v1/ocr/character (port to the ort crate with the same PaddleOCR ONNX models, or keep a Python sidecar); the numba voxel rasterizer behind dressing /image and codexes/render (needs a Rust rasterizer that matches its look; kiwi-core already has the grid decoders); Pillow sigil compositing (the image crate is fine, and PNG bytes will differ harmlessly).

summary: This area is the game-file side of TroveAPI. It mirrors Trion's update CDN into a sha256 store on disk with Mongo metadata, and serves browse/view/diff over that mirror (/v1/updates, /site/updates). After every patch it runs two pipelines: an incremental codex indexer (prefab binfabs to 8 Postgres tables, served by /v1/codexes and /site/codexes) and 33 reverse-engineered decoders that rewrite app/trove/gamedata/*.json into a shared bind-mount read by the api, web and bot containers. On top of the same blobs sit the file-format tools: SWF bitmap extraction plus JPEXS FFDec decompile, Wwise .bnk/.wem browsing plus Sound Studio rebuild, the .blueprint codec/editor/QB round-trip, a numba/numpy voxel rasterizer with a Mongo+disk payload cache, and RapidOCR (onnxruntime) stat-sheet OCR. About 25k Python lines live here (decode 9.3k, codexes 6.3k, blueprint 2.6k, updates 1.9k, audio 1.8k, swf 1.4k, render 1.4k, ocr 0.6k), plus about 2k lines of route code in app/trove/router.py and app/site/router.py. native/kiwi-core (4.2k lines of Rust, no Python types) already holds the hot kernels: the binfab wire search, zlib, Trove FNV hash, blueprint decode/encode, SWF tag/pixel parsing, the AVM2 static-array reader, wem-to-ogg/wav and .tmod. The orchestration, all 33 decoders, the codex heuristics, the rasterizer, image codecs, OCR and the HTTP layer are still Python. Porting the whole area is roughly XL: most of the effort is reproducing the decoders' and indexer's exact outputs, and two runtimes cannot become Rust code (FFDec on the JVM, and the RapidOCR model stack).

components.port_notes: Port almost one to one. The pointer is pipe-split: field 0 is the version, field 1 has 'content/' stripped, field 3 is the motd. The manifest is a 'version <tag>' line followed by 'path:sha1:size' lines parsed with rsplit(':',2); malformed lines are skipped. Python int() also accepts whitespace and '_', and a Rust port should simply skip such lines. URLs must keep the literal '//' that comes from prefix '/kiwi-live-client-patch/' plus '/public/...'. The download size is checked against the manifest. The .tfi is LEB128 records (name_len, name with NUL padding cut and '\\' turned into '/', archive_index, offset, size, fnv); LEB128 is masked to 32 bits, and a strict UTF-8 failure becomes ArchiveError. archive_size = max(offset+size), padded up to a multiple of 4, and is used as the inflate size hint. The sync is a two-level diff: manifest sha1 for loose files and dirs, then TFI FNV per logical file. Only the archiveN.tfa files that hold changed entries are downloaded. Ordinal resume: an existing in_progress version is reused. Removal of a whole dir (no .tfi left in the manifest) removes every state row with archive==dir. diff_logical and classify sort with Python's codepoint order, so plain Rust String Ord matches. Prefix range queries use $lt prefix+'￿'. backfill_last_ordinal is a $group/$max aggregate with allowDiskUse plus non-upsert bulk updates in batches of 1000. A Rust worker should run as ONE task in a single process, but keep the Redis lock while Python and Rust workers coexist. Use the same key and token semantics.

components.port_notes: Two serializers are on the wire. /v1 routes return pydantic response_models. Datetimes come out as '2026-01-02T03:04:05.123000Z' (UTC aware because Mongo runs tz_aware=True; the fraction is dropped when the microsecond is 0). The field order is the model order, and nulls are always present (e.g. FileView: branch,path,size,content_sha256,viewable,kind,reason,truncated,text,removed,removed_ordinal). /site routes hand-build dicts and use iso(), which is dt.isoformat(), giving '...+00:00'. Their key order is dict insertion order (read_file_text puts text inside base before viewable/kind/reason). Compare responses differ: v1 always has 'reason' (null) in model order branch,path,from,to,identical,is_text,reason,hunks; site omits 'reason' except when both sides are missing, and orders it identical,is_text,hunks[,reason]. Site 4xx come from HTTPException and are mapped to the envelope {error:{code,message,details:null,request_id}} through _STATUS_TO_CODE. A browser 404 on a page path gets HTML instead. v1 uses APIError codes. Cache-Control per route: versions/changes/branches/history/search max-age=30, tree/meta/view 60, compare 60 (site), vfx list 120, vfx manifest 300, vfx asset 86400 with ETag '"<sha>"' and a 304 only when If-None-Match is exactly equal (no list parsing there). /v1/updates/{branch}/file is tokenless (public_scope updates:read, rate multiplier 20) and served by Starlette FileResponse: application/octet-stream, Content-Disposition attachment; filename="<basename>" (filename*=utf-8'' when non-ASCII), ETag '"'+md5(f'{st_mtime}-{st_size}')+'"', Last-Modified, Accept-Ranges and Range support, plus Cache-Control public, max-age=86400. Removed paths resolve to their last version with removed=true and removed_ordinal. directory_listing puts dirs first and then sorts by codepoint name, rolls up file_count, size and max last_ordinal, and dir paths end in '/'. search_paths uses a Mongo $regex escaped needle with $options i, sorted by path and capped by limit, with the true total. Diff: decode_blob tries UTF-8, falls back to latin-1, then escapes C0 except \t\r\n\f plus 0x7F as \xNN. Python splitlines also splits on \f, \x85,   and  , which the port must reproduce. The 1 MiB cap per side reports 'too large'. Hunks are built from SequenceMatcher opcodes with context 3 and equal runs of 6 or fewer bridged; within a replace, removes come before adds. The manifest body is {branch,path,pkfx,deps[{ref,basename,source}],missing,game_available:true}. Reference extraction and media types come from app/trove/mods_hub/vfx.py. components.port_notes: Each decoder exposes TITLE, OUTPUT, PREFIXES, INDENT/FINAL_NEWLINE, build(tree) and count(data). The outputs are committed repo files AND are read by the Python 3.13 bot container, so the text must stay byte-identical. That means json.dumps(indent=1|4|None, ensure_ascii=False) plus an optional trailing newline. With indent the separators are ',' and ': '. With INDENT=None (items, mastery, npcs, placeables, recipes, worlds) the separators are ', ' and ': ', which serde's compact format does not produce. Keys keep dict insertion order (serde_json preserve_order/IndexMap). Floats use Python repr: shortest round-trip digits, exponent form when exp < -4 or >= 16, written 'e-05' / 'e+16'. That differs from ryu ('1e-5', '1e16') and from Rust Display (never exponent). The wire reader rounds float32 values with Python round(x,6) (kiwi-core round6 already matches) and treats wt=3 as int64 vs double by a byte-pattern heuristic. ArchiveTree lookups are case-insensitive and listings are sorted by str.lower. Some decoders bypass the native parser: recipes._components and mastery._single drive the Python _Reader/read_object directly, so in Rust those paths need kiwi-core::wire's internal reader exposed (component spans with COMPONENT_SECTIONS counts, plus the single-section reading). common.locale falls back to harvest_strings adjacency pairing. The registry's code_version is a sha1[:12] over the source of the module plus common, wire, fields, ability, codexes.localize and its transitive app.trove.decode imports. Any Rust version scheme changes every DecoderRun.code_version, which forces one full rerun after cutover (expensive: it loads prefabs/ plus the 20 MB exe). The admin status JSON (GET /admin/gamedata): {enabled,running,branch,ordinal,version_tag,decoders:[{name,title,output,state never|running|interrupted|ok|failed,code_version,serving 'rebuild'|'repo copy',last,last_ok}]}. Run dto datetimes use isoformat() ('+00:00'), with duration_ms an int. POST /admin/gamedata/run returns 409 conflict when GAMEDATA_DIR is unset, 404 for an unknown name, and {started:false,...} when a run is already going. Renew the Redis lock in Rust; the Python lock silently expires after 30 minutes. Before deleting Python, capture golden outputs for every decoder against a pinned archive ordinal; the Python modules are the only oracle.

Port each scanner exactly (harvest_strings adjacency, identity decode, quantified recipe paths, the dragon '3e AE' marker, MultiplySum '…Bonus' keys, the provider recipe-token trim against known recipe ids, and so on). The v14-v27 changelog in indexer.py lists the edge cases fixed so far. classify() maps paths under prefabs/ to codex types (most specific first; dragons are split out of mount by collection category, which refine_mount does). A blueprint resolves from the prefab ref, then block_models, then the naming-convention fallback, and is validated against the set of blueprint files and model_size > 0. When the Rust port takes over, set CODEX_PARSER_VERSION to 28 so every branch re-parses once with the Rust parser, and diff the old and new tables before switching. JSONB 'data' key order: Postgres normalizes object keys (shorter keys first, then bytewise), and Python json.loads keeps THAT order. A Rust reader must keep the server's order (serde_json preserve_order), not BTreeMap order. Floats that pass through JSONB keep their numeric text (e.g. '1.0'). models._f maps NaN and Infinity to NULL because Postgres rejects them. Stat child rows are a projection of data.stats (op string, value normalized, amount raw). The admin status shape is {branch,entry_count,parser_version,current_parser_version,rebuild:{running,started_at,finished_at,counts,error}}, with timestamps from isoformat() ('+00:00'). components.port_notes: The SQL can be reused verbatim. build_filter ANDs the conditions; search is name OR description ILIKE '%'||escaped||'%' ESCAPE '\\'; stat and ability use EXISTS subqueries; ability excludes hidden rows. SORTS is a whitelist mapping to ORDER BY (NULLS LAST plus a 'name ASC' tiebreak). The stat_value sorts need ?stat, and without it they silently fall back to name; with stat, a LEFT JOIN LATERAL picks the best value. /v1 'stat' accepts a bare name and prefixes '$Stat_'. The /site search passes stat RAW (no prefix), a behaviour difference to keep. /v1/codexes/stats fetches ALL DISTINCT ON(path) rows and sorts in Python by (value is None, -value, name) with codepoint string order, then slices offset:limit; total = count(DISTINCT path). Branch validation: v1 uses the updates BRANCHES (live-us|pts) and returns 404 'Unknown branch ...'; site returns 404 through HTTPException; the default branch is live-us. Static paths must win over /{codex_type} (axum does that natively). v1 CodexEntryOut field order: type,path,name,category,description,tradable,mastery,mastery_geode,power_rank,blueprint,data,indexed_at,stat_value,stat_percent. indexed_at from TIMESTAMPTZ serializes as '...Z' (pydantic, microsecond precision), while site _codex_row uses isoformat '+00:00' and keeps the SELECT column order codex_type,path,name,... (key 'codex_type' not 'type'; stat_value and stat_percent only when stat was given). Known quirk: pg_store.upgrade_system does not SELECT 'effects', so v1 CodexUpgradeNode.effects is always {} and the site nodes have no effects key but do include source_path. Reproduce it or fix it deliberately. /site/codexes/related emits only non-empty sections, in this order: path, crafts, ingredient, craftable_at, unlocks, member_of, made_by, used_in, unlocked_by, upgrade_cost_of, requirements (raw rows). Float formatting: /v1 is pydantic-core (1e-5 -> 0.00001, 1e-6 -> 1e-6, 1e16 -> 1e+16, 3.0 -> 3.0); /site is json.dumps repr (1e-05, 1e-06, 1e+16). The v1 router is gated by require_codexes_enabled and public_scope codexes:read (rate multiplier 5). Cache-Control (site): types/categories/stat-keys/abilities/entry/related max-age=60, search 30, upgrades 300, crafting 30. Crafting: MAX_DEPTH 20, MAX_NODES 600; craft_cost is None when any descendant is unpriced, and craft_cost_partial carries the partial sum.

Per-run -config sets decompilationTimeoutSingleMethod=15, decompilationTimeoutFile=60, exportTimeout=120, parallelSpeedUp=true, parallelSpeedUpThreadCount=2, autoDeobfuscate=true
components.port_notes: Manifest JSON (stored, then served): {swf:{version,compression none|zlib|lzma,width,height,frame_rate round(.,2),frame_count}, inventory:{shapes,sprites,fonts,texts,sounds,morphs,buttons,videos,binary,scripts} (in that key order), assets:[{id,name,source,codec,width,height,mime,bytes,sha,thumb_sha}], count}. The /site response strips sha and thumb_sha and appends 'thumb': bool at the end of each asset. Response body {branch,path,content_sha256,swf,inventory,assets,count}; Cache-Control 300. The asset route serves an ETag of the blob sha, 304 on an exact If-None-Match, media type image/png for thumbnails or the asset mime, max-age 86400. The zip route uses ETag '"<sha>-zip"', max-age 3600, Content-Disposition attachment '<stem>-assets.zip'. Zip entry names are '{id:04d}_{sanitized name}.{ext}' with _2/_3 suffixes on collision, using Unicode isalnum. The zip is capped at 256 MiB, with 413 above that. Images are sorted by char_id; at most 4000 images, 8192^2 pixels and a 256 MiB inflate per movie. The original JPEG/PNG/GIF payload is served untouched unless the JPEG tables were spliced in or an alpha plane was composited (JPEG3/4 colour is premultiplied, so it is un-premultiplied via Pillow's 'RGBa'). Name recovery walks symbol class tags (56/76) back through shapes and sprites (place tags 4/26/70). Decompile returns {scripts:[{path,size,source}] sorted by lowercased path, count, truncated, decompiler:'ffdec x.y'}, capped at 4000 scripts and 12 MiB of source and refused for movies over 24 MiB. read_header runs first and turns non-SWF input into a 422. If the decompiler is unavailable the route returns 503 service_unavailable. Bump bp_cache SWF_VERSION / SCRIPT_VERSION if Rust pixel output differs and fresh blobs are wanted. Old cached manifests stay valid because they only reference CAS shas.

components.port_notes: kiwib format: 'kiwib' + u32 version. v3/v4 is an uleb count plus svarint xyz, u16 type, BGRw bytes, and a v4 entity section. v5 is a zlib body: i32 pos[3], size[3], count, start, deltas[count-1], u16 types, u32 colours, then the entity section. Linear index L: y = L//(sx*sz), z = (L%(sx*sz))//sx, x = L%sx. An unedited voxel must round-trip byte for byte, because the encoder is handed the original (type, w). Edits are indexed against decoded order (v5 by linear index, v3/v4 by file order). Material model: the editor edits (type, w) directly; PALETTE, INTERNAL_NAMES and unknown types are preserved verbatim. QB export/import uses Troxel palettes for the _t/_a/_s maps, and the magenta attach point is written both as a voxel and as a negative matrix offset. Lint is a port of Troxel's TroveCreationsLint. Responses: inspect/model/game-model return JSON with Cache-Control no-store. Binary outputs are application/octet-stream with header X-Kiwi-Summary = json.dumps(summary), which uses Python default separators ', ' / ': ' and ensure_ascii=True; model-save also sends Content-Disposition attachment with a fallback filename. EditorError messages are wire-visible 4xx text. game-model returns 400 when a prefab stem is ambiguous ('names N different creatures. Use the full path: ...') and 404 when there are no parts.

The material map is material_for(r,g,b,w,t): types {21,18,54,55,56,24} are authored; others with max(rgb) <= 24 get _TINTS. kind S/G/E/GE has KIND_CODE 0-3; level 16+32*w for glass; spec = w for solid. PNG bytes need not be identical (cached), but visual parity with numba float math and Pillow LANCZOS is expected, so pin with golden-image tests (tests/unit/trove/test_render_voxel.py). pack_blueprint JSON: {path,count,size,x,y,z,rgb,kind,level[,spec only when any nonzero]} in voxel dict insertion order (bp_render_columns already mirrors it). Cap is 250k voxels; BlueprintTooLarge returns 413 'This blueprint is too large to preview.' and BlueprintEmpty/Error returns 422; both are remembered in the cache index, while 404 is never cached. bp_cache.respond: Cache-Control public, max-age=300; Vary Accept-Encoding; X-Kiwi-Cache hit|miss|off; Server-Timing bpcache;desc="hit" or bpcache;desc="miss";dur=<ms>; ETag '"<blob sha>"'; If-None-Match is parsed as a list with W/ stripped and returns 304 with the same headers. The gz bytes are served verbatim with Content-Encoding gzip when Accept-Encoding contains 'gzip', otherwise decompressed. JSON payload blobs are json.dumps(separators=(',',':')) with the DEFAULT ensure_ascii=True; gzip mtime is wall-clock, so blob shas are not deterministic anyway. KVX1: 'KVX1', u32 header length, header JSON with _bin:{path:[offset,count,dtype]}, zero pad to 4, then arrays (i16 x/y/z, u32 rgb, u8 kind/level/spec), each 4-byte aligned; out-of-range arrays stay in JSON. Media type application/x-kiwi-voxel. Render routes: PNG with max-age 86400. The v1 render returns 422 'Blueprint not renderable: {e}' (exception text is visible) and 404 'No blueprint ...'. A ?prefab assembled creature is all-or-nothing, falling back to the single blueprint. BRDF: ETag '"<sha>"', max-age 604800, 404 when unreadable. Version knobs to bump if Rust output differs: _RENDER_VERSION r2, _STILL_VERSION s2, PACK_VERSION v3, ASSEMBLY_VERSION a22.

components.name: Character-stat OCR
data: Disk app/trove/gamedata/character_stats.json (closed multilingual vocabulary: key, type int|percent, min, max, synonym lists)
ONNX models shipped inside the rapidocr wheel (PaddleOCR det/cls/rec)
python_deps: rapidocr (onnxruntime + opencv + pyclipper + shapely + numpy) -> 'ort' crate running the same PaddleOCR det/cls/rec ONNX models, with DBNet postprocessing (imageproc contours + clipper2 unclip) and CTC decode reimplemented; or keep a small Python/ONNX sidecar
Pillow (decode any image to RGB, LANCZOS 4x upscale strip for re-OCR) -> image + fast_image_resize
background: The engine is lazy-loaded once (thread lock); each request runs in asyncio.to_thread. The first call pays the model load
components.port_notes: Requires the ocr:read scope; the body is capped at 12 MB by the security middleware. Allowed content-types are png, jpeg, webp, gif and bmp (400 otherwise). An empty upload returns 400; engine unavailable returns 503 service_unavailable 'OCR engine is not available on this server.'; an unreadable image returns 400 via ValueError ('unreadable image: ...'). Response is CharacterStatsOcr {stats:{key:{value,unit count|percent,raw,confidence round(.,3),in_range,type_match,derived}}, matched, total_known, lines}. value is int|float with a pydantic smart union: ints stay ints, and floats keep '.0'. Parse rules: numbers match \d[\d.,]*\d\s*%? ; the last separator is a decimal point only when followed by 1-2 digits; labels are fuzzy-matched (exact 1.0, contained 0.97, else SequenceMatcher ratio >= 0.82; synonyms sorted longest first; first strict-greater wins). Pairing is type-aware, with range checks. Recovery pass: for a known stat label box with no value, re-OCR a strip (y-band of the label ±2 px, x from min-5%w to max+30%w) upscaled 4x LANCZOS, and give it confidence 0.7. Coefficient is derived via app.trove.stats when absent. The detector output (and therefore lines, order and confidence) cannot be reproduced byte-exactly outside onnxruntime+opencv, so accept the tests/unit/trove/test_ocr_eval.py accuracy fixtures as the contract. Elements are sorted by (min y, min x) of the box.

data: None

components.port_notes: kiwi-core is deliberately free of Python types, so an axum server can depend on it directly. Its convention is that None/Outcome::Abort means 'the Python reference raises or takes a different path here', and the binding falls back to Python so the exception text stays exact. In a pure-Rust server every such None needs a Rust error path, and the user-visible messages must be carried over (blueprint, wem and SWF errors surface in 422 bodies and in cached manifests). wire::parse takes a step budget (200M for the decoders, 3M for uploads) and MAX_DEPTH 1500; aborting means 'retry in Python', which will no longer exist. Either raise the budget for trusted game files or port the Python fallback semantics (the Python reader has no budget, just recursion 20000). Area-relevant modules: wire (binfab search), binfab (harvest_strings), zlib (CPython-compatible inflate/deflate), troveio (FNV), blueprint, swf, abc, audio, tmod. activity/agg/detection/renames/lbdump/gems belong to the leaderboards and gems areas. Parity is currently asserted ONLY by the Python tests in tests/unit/native, which compare against the Python reference. Before the Python reference is deleted, freeze golden fixtures (inputs plus expected outputs) as Rust tests. kiwi-py/src/lib.rs (762 lines) converts Val trees to Python objects (Obj/Repeated classes, tuples for packed, bytes for custom) and goes away.

cross_cutting_deps: Settings/config (app/core/config.py): trove_update_enabled/base_url/prefix/store_dir/probe_seconds/concurrency, gamedata_dir, mods_store_dir, trove_render_branch, trove_render_cache_ttl, trove_local_game_dir, ffdec_* (jar, java, heap, timeouts, caps, max_concurrent), postgres_enabled, codexes_rate_limit_multiplier=5, updates_file_rate_limit_multiplier=20
Mongo client with tz_aware=True (datetimes come back UTC-aware) and Beanie-equivalent index creation for update_*, decoder_runs (TTL 90d) and blueprint_cache
Postgres pool (acquire()) with a jsonb codec (json.dumps/json.loads), and startup schema init (codexes pg_schema.init runs CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS plus a DO $$ migration block)
Redis client plus Lua scripts: the leader lock (kiwi:updates:leader), the decode lock (kiwi:decode:running), the sliding-window rate limiter (rl:<key>), and the render PNG cache

Error envelope: APIError -> {error:{code,message,details,request_id}}; HTTPException mapped through _STATUS_TO_CODE; HTML 404 for browser page navigations; RequestValidationError -> 422 validation_error with jsonable_encoder(errors) in details; unhandled -> 500 internal_error
Request-ID middleware (request_id in error bodies)
Auth/scopes: require_scope('updates:read'|'ocr:read'), public_scope('updates:read', rate_multiplier=20) for /file, public_scope('codexes:read', rate_multiplier=5); get_current_superuser for /admin/*

Two JSON serializers to emulate: pydantic-core for /v1 response_model routes (datetime '...Z', floats 1e-5 -> 0.00001, 1e-6 -> 1e-6, 1e16 -> 1e+16, model field order, nulls present) and Starlette JSONResponse json.dumps (ensure_ascii=False, separators (',',':'), Python float repr 1e-05 / 1e+16, datetimes pre-stringified with isoformat '+00:00')
Starlette FileResponse semantics (ETag md5(mtime-size), Last-Modified, Range, Content-Disposition with filename* fallback)
Security middleware: per-path body caps (/v1/ocr 12 MB, /v1/mods 20 MB), CSP page allowlist
Events bus publish_type('game_update') (SSE + Discord)
app.trove.troveio (inflate/deflate/FNV/LEB128) and app.trove.tmod (.tmod read/build)
Shared content-addressed store primitive (ContentStore) used for both <trove_update_store_dir> and <mods_store_dir>
Background-task runner (FastAPI BackgroundTasks equivalent: tokio::spawn) plus a process-wide status registry (currently per-worker dicts)

Other areas this one leans on: mods_hub (assembly, rig_index, trove_layout, vfx, workshop), market.service (crafting prices), trove.stats (OCR coefficient, gamedata consumers), embed.service._read_game_file
hardest_parts: The 33 game-data decoders (~9k lines of reverse-engineered rules) must produce byte-identical gamedata/*.json, because the files are committed and are read by the Python bot and web containers. That means Python json.dumps formatting (indent 1/4/None with ', ' separators for None, ensure_ascii=False), Python float repr, dict insertion order, and the paths that call the Python wire _Reader directly (recipes._components, mastery._single), which the native parser does not expose yet

The codex indexer's heuristic byte scanners (~5.7k lines, 27 parser versions of edge-case fixes) must reproduce the same Postgres rows. Validate by force-rebuilding at CODEX_PARSER_VERSION 28 and diffing the tables. JSONB key order must keep Postgres's normalized order (serde_json preserve_order)

The only parity oracle today is the Python reference (tests/unit/native compare kiwi_native against Python). Golden fixtures must be captured for every decoder, the codex tables, the wire parses, SWF manifests, bank manifests and blueprint round-trips before any Python is removed

Exact difflib.SequenceMatcher port: get_opcodes for the file-compare hunks (autojunk=False), and ratio() for the OCR label fuzzy match. Myers/patience diff crates give different output. The port must also copy str.splitlines semantics and the latin-1 fallback

RapidOCR (onnxruntime + OpenCV + pyclipper) cannot be replicated bit-exactly. A Rust port means the 'ort' crate plus reimplemented DBNet/CTC postprocessing judged against accuracy fixtures, or a Python/ONNX sidecar
JPEXS FFDec stays on the JVM: Rust has to manage a bounded java subprocess (concurrency 2, heap cap, timeout plus process-tree kill, temp-dir isolation, output caps)

The numba/numpy voxel rasterizer and the Pillow paths (libjpeg-turbo decode, LANCZOS resize, PNG optimize, RGBa un-premultiply, DDS) can reach visual parity but not byte parity. Golden-image tolerance tests are needed, and the cache version knobs (r2/s2/v3/a22/s3) must be bumped deliberately

Wire-visible error strings that today come from Python exceptions (blueprint 422 'Blueprint not renderable: {e}', per-sound wem errors stored in cached bank manifests, SWF/decompile messages, binfab viewer messages) have to be reproduced on the Rust error paths that replace the 'native returns None, fall back to Python' convention

Datetime and float format split between /v1 (pydantic: 'Z', 0.00001, 1e+16) and /site (isoformat '+00:00', 1e-05), plus the per-route key-order and null-presence differences (e.g. compare 'reason', codex 'type' vs 'codex_type')

Decoder code_version is a hash of Python sources. Any Rust scheme triggers a one-time full rerun (prefabs/ plus the 20 MB exe) and changes DecoderRun history semantics. The decode Redis lock is never renewed (TTL 30 min)

summary: This area covers two separate HTTP surfaces. (1) The DB-less website container (app.web.main:app on trove.aallyn.net) has about 70 Jinja HTML page routes over 66 templates (61 pages and 5 partials, about 916 KB). It also serves /static with content-hash ?v= links, a host-aware robots.txt, sitemap.xml, a server-rendered first paint (app/site/ssr.py and friends, fetched from the API over internal HTTP), the regional maintenance gate (DB-IP mmdb) and the cookieless page-view collector (POST /s), which beacons batches to the API. (2) The API-side data plane (app/site/router.py, 4,267 lines) has about 190 tokenless /site/* JSON and binary routes, plus the OG, board and announcement PNG renders, the status badge and the API copy of robots/sitemap. Every one of these routes is feature-flag gated, and each is a thin wrapper over nearly every app.trove.* service. Pageview ingest and analytics (Mongo aggregation), design feedback and the geo-maintenance internal endpoint also live API-side. Roughly 13.5k Python lines plus templates. The website half is a moderate port (axum + minijinja + reqwest + maxminddb), but byte-identical HTML needs care with escaping and Python number formatting. The /site data plane is wide rather than deep, and can only land after the backend services it wraps are ported. The Pillow card renderer and the stateless tools (FFDec Java, child-process binfab reader, Wwise audio studio) are the heaviest individual pieces.

components.name: Website container shell + page-relevant middleware

starlette GZipMiddleware -> tower-http CompressionLayer with a custom predicate, or flate2

components.port_notes:
Middleware order, outermost first:
- StaticCompression: gzips only paths ending .css .js .json .svg .txt .map .md, minimum 1024 bytes. Starlette GZip uses compresslevel 9 and adds Vary: Accept-Encoding.
- request-context: echoes the X-Request-ID header or generates one. An unhandled exception becomes the 500 envelope.
- security:
  - Per-path body caps; over the cap returns 413 {"error":{"code":"bad_request","message":"Request body exceeds the N-byte limit","details":null,"request_id":...}}.
  - setdefault X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=().
  - X-Frame-Options: DENY on everything except the exact path /embed/viewer. There the header is deleted and the CSP becomes SITE_CSP minus frame-ancestors plus the allowlist from embed.service.allowed_origins, which fails closed.
  - CSP = SITE_CSP when the path is in _PAGE_PATHS, starts with /static/ or /site/, or matches _PAGE_PREFIXES (/mods/ /modpacks/ /player/ /drop/ /swf-docs/). Otherwise API_CSP. Both strings must be copied verbatim.
  - /static/* Cache-Control is OVERWRITTEN by static_version.cache_control: "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" when ?v equals the current hash, "public, max-age=604800" for .woff2, else "no-cache".
  - Page paths get setdefault "no-cache".
  - Any request with an Authorization header or a kiwi_site_access cookie gets Cache-Control OVERWRITTEN to "private, no-store" and Vary merged with "Cookie, Authorization", except public assets (/site/rigs/, /site/dressing/, /site/render/brdf-map.png, /site/codexes/render).
- geo gate.
- HEAD->GET for routing only. The scope is copied, never mutated in place, and /v1/events is excluded.

static_version:
- Every rendered page is post-processed with the regex (\s(?:src|href)=")(/static/[^"?#]+?(?<!\.woff2)(?<!\.woff))("), which appends ?v= + sha256(file bytes).hexdigest()[:10].
- Only applied when the resolved file stays under the static root and exists.
- The hash is cached by (mtime_ns, size).

Themed HTML 404:
- Uses the exact inline _NOT_FOUND_HTML (it has a data: favicon).
- Served when status is 404, the method is GET or HEAD, the path does NOT start with any of /v1/, /v1, /admin, /site/, /git/, /secret-scanning, /openapi, /.well-known, /health, /config, /metrics, and the Accept header contains text/html.
- Note that "/v1" as a bare prefix also catches /v1foo.
- Otherwise the JSON envelope is returned, with code from the status map (404 -> not_found). A bare HTTPException(404) has message "Not Found" (the HTTP phrase).

Starlette StaticFiles traps:
- ETag is '"' + md5(f"{mtime}-{size}") + '"', plus Last-Modified.
- Answers 304 on If-None-Match or If-Modified-Since.
- Content-Type comes from Python mimetypes, and text/* types get "; charset=utf-8".
- A missing file raises HTTPException(404), which serves the HTML 404 page to browsers because /static/ is not an API prefix.

/gamedata/{name}:
- Allowlist is pvp.json, gem_upgrades.json, gear.json. Anything else is HTTPException(404).
- FileResponse with media_type application/json and "Cache-Control: public, max-age=300". The file wins from gamedata_dir when present. Starlette adds an etag and supports Range.

openapi_url is None. The lifespan starts the beacon and the GeoIP ASN loop.

components.port_notes:
Every page router call depends on web_flags.resolve:
- Fetches /site/feature-flags (5s memo).
- Sets every flag on request state.
- Returns 404 via feature_blocks; browsers get the HTML 404 page.

Template context:
- Context processors add the 42 SITE_FEATURE_FLAGS booleans (default True), nav_menu and nav_active (from search_index), design/theme/vx_tod (appearance), and `request`. navbar.html reads request.url.path.
- appearance: btt_design must be voxel or classic (default voxel). btt_theme must be auto, light or dark (default auto). vx_tod comes from the Trove hour (UTC-11): 5-8 morning, 9-16 day, 17-19 dusk, otherwise night. light pins day and dark pins night.
- GET / picks index.html for classic, otherwise home_voxel.html, and sets Vary: Cookie.
- Responses are text/html; charset=utf-8, and the body is post-processed by static_version.link.

Jinja traps for minijinja:
- Autoescape differs from markupsafe:
  - markupsafe emits " and ' and leaves '/' alone.
  - minijinja emits " and ' and escapes '/' as /.
  - Escaped '/' would break the /static ?v= regex on any templated href, so a markupsafe-compatible formatter is required.
- `| tojson` is json.dumps(sort_keys=True), with < > & ' escaped as < > & '.
- `| urlencode` uses safe='/'.
- Filters in use: default, safe, join, length, upper, replace, urlencode, tojson.
- 2 macros in partials/class_detail.html.
- The templates use Python method calls: r.sort_values.items() and _p.startswith('/mods/').
- Python truthiness applies, and floats render as Python str (350.0).

Per-route behaviour:
- OG and JSON-LD:
  - _ld() is json.dumps({"@context":"https://schema.org", **data}, ensure_ascii=False). Default separators are ', ' and ': ', and then '<' becomes <.
  - _plain_excerpt regexes, desc[:300] (Python code-point slicing).
  - og_image is {api}/site/mods/image/{banner_sha or first preview}, else favicon. twitter_card is summary_large_image only when an image exists.
- /mods/{handle} returns 404 whenever the internal fetch fails or the result is not a dict.
- /browse sorts by re.sub(r'^\W+','',title or slug).lower(), where \W is Unicode-aware.
- /embed/viewer whitelists backdrop (melee|pistol|staff|spear|fist|hat), mode (auto|blueprint|assembled|vfx|audio) and theme (dark|light).
- /activity?period lowercases the value against 7d and 1m and drives the og:image query string.
- /swf-docs/{doc}:
  - A case-insensitive README redirects 301 to /swf-docs.
  - A non-canonical slug redirects 301 to the canonical one.
  - An unknown slug is 404.
  - markdown is rendered with html disabled, then sibling links are rewritten with href="(?:\./)?([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\.md(#[^"]*)?" -> /swf-docs/<slug>.
  - The doc_updated stamp uses strftime '%d %b %Y, %H:%M UTC'.
- Route order: /mods/why must win over /mods/{handle}. matchit gives static segments priority, so this works.

components.port_notes:
The builders are transport-agnostic: fetch(path, params) returns the same JSON the /site proxies emit, or None. Every builder degrades to {} or [].

Memo key: path + '?' + '&'.join(f'{k}={v}' over sorted params). Python str() is used for the values.

Formatting traps, which matter only for byte-identical HTML:
- num(): ints use f'{int(v):,}'. Non-integral floats use f'{v:,.2f}' with trailing zeros and the dot stripped. bool or non-number gives '—'.
- date(): time.strftime('%d %b %Y', gmtime). datetime_attr: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'. ISO strings are parsed with fromisoformat after Z -> +00:00.
- text(): strips tags, links and md markers, collapses whitespace, slices to `limit` code points, then rstrip + '…'.
- _release_file uses Python round(), which is banker's rounding (Rust: f64::round_ties_even), and :.1f MB.
- class_activity share is f'{share*100:.1f}%' and rows are sorted by active_players descending (stable).
- classes_page:
  - _fmt_stat uses ',' grouping and .2f trimming.
  - _sheet_at uses round(v,2), banker's rounding on the binary value.
  - Stages use f'{mult*100:g}%' and f'+{base:g}'.
  - :g means 6 significant digits, exponent form when exp < -4 or >= 6 ('1.5e+06'). This needs a hand-written formatter.
- abilities/allies:
  - :g formatting.
  - _LEAD regex with re.S|re.I.
  - .title() on the label.
  - allies rows sorted by name.lower() and stats by sorted(seen) (code-point order).
  - slug regex [^a-z0-9]+.
- mod_stats_view groups by title.partition(' - ') in the order Zakros UI, Zakros FX, Zakros BP, then the rest alphabetically. Mods within a group are sorted by title.lower(). It emits ItemList JSON-LD (ensure_ascii=False, then < -> <).
- mod_related_view sorts by (not same-line, -download_count).
- market_view uses the key item_names, not items: Jinja attribute lookup would otherwise resolve dict.items. minijinja has no such clash, but keep the key names.
- hubs.HUBS titles contain raw HTML and are rendered with |safe.
- commands_view mirrors commands.js exactly: chips cover all categories, sections only the non-empty ones, and search is syntax + aliases + desc + note lowercased.

- The web version is "public, max-age=600" and pages at 100. The API version is "public, max-age=3600", pages at 1000 and caps at 25,000 per section.

/site/feature-flags:
- Plain JSON object.
- Key order is SITE_FEATURE_FLAGS insertion order (42 keys, starting mods_hub_enabled ... ending community_sites_enabled), then cheater_detection_enabled, alt_clusters_enabled, renames_enabled, duplicates_enabled.
- apply_derived forces dressing_room_page_enabled = page AND master.
- "public, max-age=5".

feature_blocks path rules must be copied exactly, including one QUIRK: when abilities/guides/allies/gem_tools are disabled the function does `return False`. Those pages are never 404'd, and the check short-circuits the remaining rules for those exact paths.

API side: every route on the site router, including robots, the sitemap, OG PNGs and the badge, first resolves all 42 flags and raises HTTPException(404). The default detail "Not Found" goes into the JSON envelope.

components.name: Site-wide search + navbar page registry
data: Postgres codex_entry (+ codex_* via codexes_read.query_entries)

Mongo mod_projects / modpack_projects (list_public with q)
Mongo runtime_config (flags)
python_deps: unicodedata.normalize('NFKD') + combining strip + str.casefold -> unicode-normalization + caseless (casefold differs from to_lowercase, e.g. ß -> ss)
components.port_notes:
Query params:
- q (default '').
- subject (optional).
- limit (1-100, default 30).
- offset (>=0).
- branch, which must be live-us or pts. Anything else is 404 with detail "Unknown branch 'x' (known: live-us, pts)".

Response:
- {query, subjects:[{key,label,count}], subject, items:[{...row, subject}], count, total}, "public, max-age=15".
- Query < 2 characters, or no subjects available, returns the empty shape with subjects [].
- Preview mode (no subject): each subject is fetched at 4 rows. Only subjects with a non-zero count are listed, and total is the sum of counts.
- Subject mode: subjects lists ALL available subjects with counts (count = max(preview total, paged total)).

Subject order: pages, collections, items, recipes, styles, players, mods, modpacks. Each subject's flag gate comes from _SUBJECT_FLAG. An unknown flag counts as OFF in the search map but as ON in nav_menu (via .get(flag, False)).

Pages scoring:
- 100 exact, 80 prefix, 60 token-prefix, 40 substring, 25 keyword, 20 all-words.
- Sort key is (-score, tabs after pages, name) with a code-point name compare. Capped at 200, then sliced by offset/limit.

Row shapes:
- Page row: {name,path,icon,group,parent,kind:'page'|'tab'}.
- Codex row: {name, path:'/codexes#type='+quote(type,safe='')+'&q='+quote(name,safe=''), detail:category, kind:codex_type, image:'/site/codexes/render?dim=64&blueprint='+quote(bp,safe='') or None}. A multi-type subject is queried once without a type filter and then filtered in Python, so its count is the unfiltered total.
- Player row: path '/player/'+quote(name,safe='').
- Mods/modpacks row: path '/{mods|modpacks}/{handle}/{slug}', image '/site/mods/image/{sha}?w=200'.

quote() uses Python's always-safe set (A-Za-z0-9_.-~). A subject that throws returns ([],0).

The search flag map adds cheater_detection_enabled, alt_clusters_enabled and leaderboard_renames_enabled (note: a different key from renames_enabled).

nav_menu groups are Live, Economy, Plan, Create, Learn. nav_is_active does prefix matching but excludes '/'.
